Fractal Academic Framework & Pedagogical Architecture
FRACTAL ACADEMICS
The recent developments in the subject areas along with the innovation in Course structuring like ‘Fractal Academics’ and ‘Skill Orientation’
were incorporated in the Curriculum design in IIIT Naya Raipur. The innovative idea of ‘Fractal Academics’ though originated from Carnegie
Melon University USA is being implemented in some of the new IITs in India as well.
IIIT NR has embedded issues like ‘Job-Orientation’ and ‘Research Enabling' as the driving force behind the Curriculum development, while
encouraging the entrepreneurial instinct in the students.
The IIITNR Senate proposed a design of such curriculum which while making students Industry ready, also enables them to get into
“Undergraduate Researching”. It is being endeavored to encourage the students in their Minor and Major project work to undertake
research-oriented problems so that they may get exposed to many of the prevailing Science and Technology problems while supporting
Faculty members in their Project/Research work as well.
Fractal academic supports to offer a course with less credit, minimum of one credit instead of courses with large credit in conventional
curriculum system. This smaller credit subject is very useful to introduce industry related emerging subject. It facilitates T-Education model
for both breadth and depth of knowledge.
The academics at IlIT Naya Raipur provides an optimum mixture of academics, research, and industry. We are always eager to learn and
try to incorporate new things in our flexible curriculum.
The salient features of the Curriculum of IlITNR are:
Skill First, Theory Later, Projects Integrated
Fractal Academics, that enables offering of courses with smaller credits
Learning by Doing Model
Fosters project-based learning
Exposure to both hardware + software in IT Workshops
Allows learning by application of theory
Enables development of both professional skills + technical skills
Fosters interdisciplinary skills and wider knowledge enrichment
Enables to cope up with fast changing IT revolution
Facilitates T-Education model for both breadth and depth of knowledge
Engineering courses right from First semester instead of 12th ++ courses in First year
High Industry-linkages

B.Tech Overall Curriculum Flowchart
B.TECH CURRICULUM
DSPM-IIITNR currently runs three undergraduate programs: B.Tech. in Computer Science & Engineering (CSE) , B.Tech. in Electronics &
Communication Engineering (ECE) and BTech. in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) . These credit-based programs are
designed to foster core skills with innovation and entrepreneurship skills among students. The dynamic structure of the curriculum
orchestrates with the changing needs of industry and academia. IlIT Naya Raipur follows the Fractal Curriculum.

M.Tech Overall Curriculum Flowchart
M.TECH CURRICULUM
M.Tech. program of the Institute is open to all Indian Nationals in the following specializations:
Computer Science and Engineering (Intake :20 seats)
Specializations: (a) Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
(b) Information Security
Electronics and Communication Engineering (Intake :20 seats)
Specializations: (a) Communication and Signal Processing
(b) VLSI and Embedded System
Some key features of M. Tech. program in IlIT-NR are listed below.
IIT-NR is mentored by a highly eminent board consisting of Mr. Ajai Chowdhry (Founder-HCL), Prof. Arogyaswami Paulraj (Marconi
Award winner & Professor Emeritus-Stanford University) and other visionaries from Academia and Industry.
IIIT-NR is committed to bringing to the Institute the best of the faculty and resources to enable students create solutions for today's
problems and products for the needs of the country, esp. the underprivileged.
Admissions in M.Tech. program is strictly based on valid GATE score.
Eligible Applicants admitted to M.Tech. programme will receive a monthly Institute scholarship of Rs.12,400/-.
Students are encouraged to present research papers at reputed conferences and for which the institute supports financially as per the
norms of IIIT Naya Raipur.
One Semester research abroad with institute financial assistantship up to 5 Lakhs for selected candidates.

Ph.D. Academic Framework and Timeline
PH.D
IIT Naya Raipur offers admission to the Ph.D. Programs in CSE, ECE,DSAI, Physics, Mathematics and Humanities. The goal of the Ph.D.
program at llIT-NR is to prepare the scholars for becoming global academic, industrial and R&D leaders.
Some key features of Ph.D. program in IlIT-NR are listed below.
IIIT-NR emphasizes to align its R&D focus to achieve the goal of technological self-reliance. Faculties and research scholars conduct
research projects in several emerging areas of engineering, Science & Technology, and Management etc. The institute has ongoing
< academic and research collaborations with many national and international universities, governments and industries in order to
keep pace with expanding frontiers of knowledge and global developments.
Research scholars are encouraged to propose product or service based ideas useful to society and are encouraged to build working
prototypes of these products. The institute involves exploration of some of the impacts of new technologies on society, usually the
< unprivileged ones.
privilegs
Research scholars admitted to Ph.D. program under regular Institute Scholar scheme (full time) are eligible for the Institute
Teaching/Research Assistantship.
Research scholars are encouraged to present research papers at reputed conferences and attend eminent workshops in their
respective research area. For this, the institute supports financially as per the norms of IlIT Naya Raipur.

About IIIT-NR Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR) is a premier state-funded institute established in 2015 under the International Institute of Information Technology University Act, 2013 of the Government of Chhattisgarh. The institute is a joint initiative of the Government of Chhattisgarh and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited, a Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. Incorporated as a state university and recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), IIIT-NR is committed to pursuing excellence in higher education, research, and development in Information Technology (IT) and associated disciplines. The institute firmly believes in knowledge dissemination and in imparting entrepreneurial skills to its students, enabling them to address real-world problems with confidence and creativity. The institute is housed on a fully residential, fifty-acre green campus in Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar) — India's first planned green and smart city — approximately 23 km from Raipur and well connected by air, rail, and road. The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal space for innovation and learning. IIIT-NR offers undergraduate (B.Tech.), postgraduate (M.Tech.), and doctoral (Ph.D.) programmes in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), and Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI). These credit-based programmes are designed to foster core competence together with innovation and entrepreneurship, with a dynamic curriculum structure that keeps pace with the changing needs of industry and academia. Vision of the Institute To be a globally recognized institution of excellence in information technology and allied disciplines, nurturing innovators, entrepreneurs, and socially responsible technologists who contribute to national and global development. Mission of the Institute • To impart high-quality, value-based, and outcome-oriented technical education. • To foster state-of-the-art, interdisciplinary research and product development. • To cultivate entrepreneurial mind-sets and industry-ready professional skills. • To engage with society and industry for sustainable and inclusive growth. B.Tech CSE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR 2. About the Department of CSE The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) at IIIT-NR offers a four-year Bachelor of Technology programme that builds a strong foundation in the theory and practice of computing — spanning programming, data structures and algorithms, systems, databases, networks, and the rapidly growing areas of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science. The programme combines rigorous fundamentals with extensive hands-on laboratory work, design projects, and industry-aligned skills so that graduates are equipped to design, build, and reason about complex software and computing systems. The department is taught by highly qualified and research-active faculty whose expertise spans artificial intelligence and machine learning, data science, computer networks and security, distributed and cloud systems, theoretical computer science, computer vision, and software engineering. Every semester integrates project-based learning, supported by well-equipped computing laboratories, high-performance computing resources, and the active mentorship of research scholars. AI-assisted full-stack prototyping is embedded from the first year, reflecting the institute's emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship. Vision of the Department To emerge as a centre of excellence in computer science and engineering education and research, producing globally competent engineers, innovators, and entrepreneurs capable of solving complex computing problems for the benefit of society. Mission of the Department
To provide a rigorous, outcome-based foundation in computer science and engineering with strong hands-on, design, and problem-solving exposure.
To promote research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, data science, cyber-security, and distributed and intelligent systems.
To inculcate professional ethics, lifelong learning, and social responsibility among students.
To build strong linkages with industry, research organizations, and the wider community for mutually beneficial collaboration. Programme Offered B.Tech. in Computer Science and Engineering — 4 years / 8 semesters, 160 credits, with multiple entry- exit options, multidisciplinary minors, an Honors track, and a strong project and internship component, in line with NEP 2020 and the NBA outcome-based education framework. Credit Structure and Break-up The programme follows the NEP-based B.Tech. Common Format credit scheme, with a total programme credit requirement of 160 credits distributed across Lecture (L), Tutorial (T), Practical (P), and Scholarly Engagement Hours (S) components as defined below: Credit Component (as per NEP-based Definition / Contact-Hour Equivalence B.Tech. Detailed Course-wise Syllabus (Core Subjects) This section presents the detailed Outcome-Based Education (OBE) syllabus for the core (compulsory) courses of the programme, covering the Basic Science (BSC), Engineering Science (ESC), Programme Core (PCC), and Programme Specific Core (PSC) courses from Semester 1 to Semester 6. Each course is described using a uniform OBE template comprising: course information, Course Outcomes (COs), a five-module detailed syllabus with contact hours, text and reference books, industry relevance, Open Educational Resources (OERs) and open repositories, suggested laboratory exercises, and recommended open-source simulators/tools. Professional (Programme) Electives and Open Electives are listed separately in Sections 7 and 8. Value- added, HSMC, and skill courses follow institute-wide common syllabi and are reflected in the scheme. Multidisciplinary Minor (MDM) streams are excluded as per the scope of this book. B.Tech CSE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR MA-L-01-C Linear Algebra and Matrix Analysis
Course Code MA-L-01-C Credits 3
Structure (L-T-P- Category BSC (Basic Science) 2-1-0-0
S)
Prerequisite Nil Laboratory No Provides the matrix-algebraic and vector-space foundation underpinning signal processing, communications, control, machine learning, and numerical computation in electronics engineering. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Solve systems of linear equations using Gaussian elimination and matrix inversion. CO2 Carry out matrix operations including inverses, rank, and determinants. CO3 Determine eigenvalues and eigenvectors and solve eigenvalue problems. CO4 Apply matrix algebra to linear transformations and change of basis. CO5 Demonstrate understanding of inner-product spaces, orthonormalization, and SVD. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Content Hours Systems of Linear Equations M1 System of linear equations; Gaussian elimination; inverse and rank of a matrix by 5 elementary transformations; properties and applications of determinants. Vector Spaces M2 Vector spaces over real and complex fields; subspaces; linear dependence and 6 independence; spanning set; basis and dimension. Linear Transformations M3 Linear transformations and their matrices; kernel and range; change of basis; rank- 6 nullity theorem; matrix representation. Eigenvalues & Diagonalization M4 Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; characteristic polynomial; diagonalization of matrices; 6 Cayley-Hamilton theorem and applications. Inner Product Spaces & SVD M5 Inner product spaces; norms; orthogonality; Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization; Singular 5 Value Decomposition (SVD) and applications. Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 28 Text Books
S. Lipschutz, M. Lipson, Schaum's Outlines of Linear Algebra, McGraw-Hill.
G. Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 4th ed., Wellesley-Cambridge Press, 2009. Reference Books

Course Code MA-L-02-C Credits 3
Structure (L-T-P- Category BSC (Basic Science) 2-1-0-0
S)
Prerequisite Nil Laboratory No Develops single- and multivariable calculus tools essential for modelling continuous systems, optimization, and field theory in engineering. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Find limits of functions graphically, numerically, and algebraically. CO2 Apply continuity and differentiability to algebraic and transcendental functions. CO3 Use partial derivatives, gradients, and Lagrange multipliers for optimization. CO4 Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate definite integrals. CO5 Evaluate multiple integrals to solve area, volume, and real-world problems. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Content Hours Single-Variable Calculus Review M1 Limit, continuity and differentiability; indeterminate forms and L'Hospital rule; Mean 5 Value theorem; Maclaurin and Taylor series. Functions of Several Variables M2 Limits and continuity; partial derivatives and differentiability; linearization and 6 differentials; chain rule; gradient vector; tangent planes; directional derivatives. Multivariable Optimization M3 Extreme values and saddle points; Lagrange multipliers; Taylor's formula for several 5 variables; partial derivatives with constrained variables. Double Integrals M4 Double integrals; change of order of integration; area and volume by double integral; 6 double integrals in polar form. Triple Integrals M5 Triple integrals in rectangular, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates; substitutions in 6 multiple integrals; applications. Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 28 Text Books

Structure (L-T-P- Category ESC / VSEC 2-0-2-2

Prerequisite Nil Laboratory Mandatory (2 Hours) Builds algorithmic problem-solving ability and procedural programming skills in C, the foundation for embedded and systems programming in electronics. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Identify and list the programming tasks involved in a computational problem. CO2 Implement conditional branching, iteration, and recursion in C. CO3 Use arrays, pointers, and structures to develop algorithms and programs. CO4 Apply dynamic memory allocation and file handling in C. CO5 Design modular C programs using functions and good coding practices. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. B.Tech CSE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR EC-L-01-C Digital Electronics using Verilog
Course Code EC-L-01-C Credits 3
Structure (L-T-P- Category ESC (Engineering Science) 2-0-2-0
S)
Prerequisite Nil Laboratory Mandatory (2 Hours) Introduces digital logic design and hardware description using Verilog HDL, forming the gateway to VLSI, FPGA, and embedded design. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Understand number systems, logic gates, Boolean simplification, and flip-flops. CO2 Design basic digital systems using standard ICs and Verilog. CO3 Analyse and design combinational circuits. CO4 Analyse and design sequential circuits including counters and FSMs. CO5 Implement and simulate digital designs in Verilog HDL. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Content Hours Number Systems & Boolean Algebra M1 Number systems and conversions; logic gates and truth tables; Boolean algebra; K- 5 maps; NAND/NOR implementations; tabular (Quine-McCluskey) simplification. Combinational Design - Arithmetic M2 Design procedure; half/full adder and subtractor; 4-bit ripple-carry adder; carry-look- 6 ahead adder; BCD arithmetic. Combinational Design - MSI M3 Decoders, encoders, multiplexers, de-multiplexers, magnitude comparators; 5 implementing logic with MUX/decoders. Sequential Circuits M4 Latches and flip-flops; FF conversions; serial and parallel shift registers; synchronous 6 and asynchronous counter design. FSM & Verilog HDL M5 Mealy and Moore machines; state diagrams and tables; Verilog modelling styles (gate, 6 dataflow, behavioral); test benches and simulation. Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 28 Text Books

Prerequisite Nil Laboratory No Introduces the principles and formalism of quantum mechanics that underpin modern electronics, photonics, semiconductor devices, and quantum technologies. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Use the language and formalism of basic quantum mechanics. M1 6
density; Schrödinger formalism; time-dependent and time-independent equations; eigenstates, eigenvalues, expectation values. Hydrogen Atom M4 Solution of the Schrödinger equation in a central potential; hydrogen-like atom; quantum 5 numbers and applications. Course Code MA-L-03-C Credits 3
Structure (L-T-P- Category BSC (Basic Science) 2-1-0-0
S)
Prerequisite Nil Laboratory No Provides probability and statistical inference tools essential for communication theory, signal processing, reliability, and machine learning. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Apply probability rules including additive/multiplicative laws and Bayes' rule. CO2 Analyse data using measures of central tendency, dispersion, and location. CO3 Identify and use discrete and continuous distributions. CO4 Translate real-world problems into probability models. CO5 Perform estimation and hypothesis testing. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Content Hours Probability Foundations M1 Axiomatic definition; finite sample spaces; joint and conditional probability; 6 independence; total probability; Bayes' rule and applications. Random Variables Discrete and continuous random variables; cdf, pmf, pdf and properties; bivariate and
M2 6
multivariate random variables; jointly distributed random variables; conditional and joint densities. Distributions & CLT M3 Standard discrete and continuous distributions; sampling and sampling distributions; 6 Central Limit Theorem. Descriptive Statistics M4 Measures of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, kurtosis; data representation: 5 histogram, pie chart, box-plot, bi-plot, multidimensional scaling. Inference M5 Methods of estimation; unbiased estimators; confidence intervals (Z, t); hypothesis 5 testing; types of errors; rejection-region and p-value approaches. Finite Automata and Formal Prerequisite Laboratory Mandatory Languages, Data Structures Covers the phases of compilation: lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate code, optimization, and code generation. Course Outcomes (COs) On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to: CO Statement CO1 Explain the structure and phases of a compiler. CO2 Design lexical analysers using regular expressions. CO3 Apply parsing techniques for context-free grammars. CO4 Apply syntax-directed translation and semantic analysis. CO5 Apply intermediate-code generation and optimization. Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules) Mod. Content Hours Introduction & Lexical Analysis M1 Phases of a compiler; lexical analysis; tokens and patterns; finite automata for scanners; 5 lexer generators (lex/flex). Syntax Analysis M2 Context-free grammars; top-down parsing (recursive descent, LL(1)); bottom-up parsing 6 (LR, SLR, LALR); parser generators (yacc). Semantic Analysis M3 Syntax-directed definitions; attribute grammars; type checking; symbol tables; scope 5 handling. Intermediate Code & Runtime M4 Intermediate representations; three-address code; runtime environments; activation 5 records; storage organization. Optimization & Code Generation M5 Code optimization techniques; basic blocks and flow graphs; register allocation; target 5 code generation. Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 26 Text Books

A. NSS (Hours of Service): NSS Coordinator will be responsible for providing the grade Grade A+ A B+ B C+ C F Hours of ≥ 240 200-239 180-199 140-179 100-139 60-99 <60 service B. Students can attend any one activity to earn the grade. b. If a student wants to increase their grade, they need to participate in another activity also. Then the final grade will be decided by combining the grades of the two activities (NSS and ISR). For example, If a student scores an A in NSS and a C in ISR, his final grade will be A+. In general, students will be given one grade above the maximum grade of two activities, provided both grades are C and above. c. For an F grade, the student has to do all ISR activities in the next semester.

Sports activities: participation in institute sports activities and sports competition: The SAC president will be responsible for providing the participant's name c. Attend IEEE activities and institute talk: The IEEE Coordinator will be responsible for providing the name d. Volunteers in different technical and non-technical events. The faculty coordinator of particular activities will be responsible for providing the participant's name. All activities will have equal weightage. About IIIT-NR
Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR) is
a premier state-funded institute established in 2015 under the International Institute of Information
Technology University Act, 2013 of the Government of Chhattisgarh. The institute is a joint initiative of the
Government of Chhattisgarh and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited, a Maharatna
Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Power, Government of India.
Incorporated as a state university and recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and
approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), IIIT-NR is committed to pursuing
excellence in higher education, research, and development in Information Technology (IT) and associated
disciplines. The institute firmly believes in knowledge dissemination and in imparting entrepreneurial skills
to its students, enabling them to address real-world problems with confidence and creativity.
The institute is housed on a fully residential, fifty-acre green campus in Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar) —
India's first planned green and smart city — approximately 23 km from Raipur and well connected by air,
rail, and road. The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating
an ideal space for innovation and learning.
IIIT-NR offers undergraduate (B.Tech.), postgraduate (M.Tech.), and doctoral (Ph.D.) programmes in
Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), and Data
Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI). These credit-based programmes are designed to foster core
competence together with innovation and entrepreneurship, with a dynamic curriculum structure that
keeps pace with the changing needs of industry and academia.
Vision of the Institute
To be a globally recognized institution of excellence in information technology and allied disciplines,
nurturing innovators, entrepreneurs, and socially responsible technologists who contribute to national and
global development.
Mission of the Institute
• To impart high-quality, value-based, and outcome-oriented technical education.
• To foster state-of-the-art, interdisciplinary research and product development.
• To cultivate entrepreneurial mind-sets and industry-ready professional skills.
• To engage with society and industry for sustainable and inclusive growth.

B.Tech DSAI Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR
About the Department of DSAI
The Department of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) at IIIT-NR offers a four-year Bachelor of
Technology programme that builds a strong foundation in computing and then develops deep
specialization in data science, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. Alongside a solid core of
programming, data structures, algorithms, databases, and systems, the programme provides rigorous
training in statistics, optimization, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural-language
processing, reinforcement learning, and the emerging areas of generative and agentic AI. The curriculum
combines mathematical depth with extensive hands-on practice so that graduates can design, build, and
reason about intelligent, data-driven systems.
The department is taught by highly qualified and research-active faculty whose expertise spans machine
learning and deep learning, data science and analytics, computer vision, natural-language processing,
reinforcement learning, statistical modelling, and trustworthy and responsible AI. Every semester
integrates project-based learning, supported by well-equipped computing laboratories, GPU/high-
performance computing resources, and the active mentorship of research scholars. AI-assisted full-stack
prototyping is embedded from the first year, reflecting the institute's emphasis on innovation and
entrepreneurship.
Vision of the Department
To emerge as a centre of excellence in data science and artificial intelligence education and research,
producing globally competent engineers, innovators, and entrepreneurs capable of building intelligent,
data-driven, and responsible solutions for the benefit of society.
Mission of the Department
To provide a rigorous, outcome-based foundation in data science and artificial intelligence with
strong mathematical, computational, and hands-on exposure.
To promote research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in emerging areas such as deep learning,
computer vision, natural-language processing, and generative and agentic AI.
To inculcate professional ethics, responsible-AI practices, lifelong learning, and social responsibility
among students.
To build strong linkages with industry, research organizations, and the wider community for mutually
beneficial collaboration.
Programme Offered
B.Tech. in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence — 4 years / 8 semesters, 160 credits, with multiple
entry-exit options, multidisciplinary minors, an Honors track, and a strong project and internship
component, in line with NEP 2020 and the NBA outcome-based education framework.
Credit Structure and Break-up
The programme follows the NEP-based B.Tech. Common Format credit scheme, with a total programme
credit requirement of 160 credits distributed across Lecture (L), Tutorial (T), Practical (P), and Scholarly
Engagement Hours (S) components as defined below:

Salient Features of the Curriculum
• Choice-based credit system with Programme Electives (Cloud Computing, Networking, IoT, and
Robotics tracks), Open Electives, and Multidisciplinary Minors.
• Strong AI/ML spine: AI Foundations, Applied ML, Pattern Recognition, Deep Learning, Computer
Vision, NLP, Reinforcement Learning, and Generative & Agentic AI.
• AI-assisted full-stack prototyping, IoT, 3D printing, and hardware-prototyping skills embedded from
the first year.
• Strong project spine: Mini Project, Project-I & II (with research methodology), Minor & Major Projects,
and a mandatory summer internship.
• Honors option (additional 15 credits) for high-performing students with a research publication / patent
requirement.
• Value-added courses on Indian Knowledge Systems, ethics, constitution, finance, and community
service for holistic development.

Outcome-Based Education (OBE) Framework
The B.Tech. (DSAI) curriculum is designed and delivered following the Outcome-Based Education (OBE)
philosophy advocated by the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) and consistent with the Washington
Accord. Under OBE, the curriculum, teaching-learning processes, and assessment are aligned to clearly
defined outcomes at three levels — Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs), Programme Outcomes
(POs) with Programme Specific Outcomes (PSOs), and Course Outcomes (COs).

Attainment is measured through direct assessment (continuous internal evaluation, end-semester

alumni, and employer surveys). The closed feedback loop drives continuous quality improvement (CQI).

This section presents the detailed Outcome-Based Education (OBE) syllabus for the core (compulsory) courses
of the programme, covering the Basic Science (BSC), Engineering Science (ESC), Programme Core (PCC),
and Programme Specific Core (PSC) courses from Semester 1 to Semester 6. Each course is described using
a uniform OBE template comprising: course information, Course Outcomes (COs), a five-module detailed
syllabus with contact hours, text and reference books, industry relevance, Open Educational Resources
(OERs) and open repositories, suggested laboratory exercises, and recommended open-source
simulators/tools.
Professional (Programme) Electives and Open Electives are listed separately in Sections 7 and 8. Value-
added, HSMC, and skill courses follow institute-wide common syllabi and are reflected in the scheme.
Multidisciplinary Minor (MDM) streams are excluded as per the scope of this book.

MA-L-01-C Linear Algebra and Matrix Analysis
Course Code MA-L-01-C Credits 3
Structure (L-T-P-
Category BSC (Basic Science) 2-1-0-0
S)
Prerequisite Nil Laboratory No
Provides the matrix-algebraic and vector-space foundation underpinning signal processing, communications,
control, machine learning, and numerical computation in electronics engineering.
Course Outcomes (COs)
On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to:
CO Statement
CO1 Solve systems of linear equations using Gaussian elimination and matrix inversion.
CO2 Carry out matrix operations including inverses, rank, and determinants.
CO3 Determine eigenvalues and eigenvectors and solve eigenvalue problems.
CO4 Apply matrix algebra to linear transformations and change of basis.
CO5 Demonstrate understanding of inner-product spaces, orthonormalization, and SVD.
Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules)
Mod. Content Hours
Systems of Linear Equations
M1 System of linear equations; Gaussian elimination; inverse and rank of a matrix by 5
elementary transformations; properties and applications of determinants.
Vector Spaces
M2 Vector spaces over real and complex fields; subspaces; linear dependence and 6
independence; spanning set; basis and dimension.
Linear Transformations
M3 Linear transformations and their matrices; kernel and range; change of basis; rank- 6
nullity theorem; matrix representation.
Eigenvalues & Diagonalization
M4 Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; characteristic polynomial; diagonalization of matrices; 6
Cayley-Hamilton theorem and applications.
Inner Product Spaces & SVD
M5 Inner product spaces; norms; orthogonality; Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization; Singular 5
Value Decomposition (SVD) and applications.
Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 28
Text Books
S. Lipschutz, M. Lipson, Schaum's Outlines of Linear Algebra, McGraw-Hill.
G. Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 4th ed., Wellesley-Cambridge Press, 2009.
Reference Books
J. Defranza, D. Gagliardi, Introduction to Linear Algebra with Applications, McGraw-Hill.
K. Hoffman, R. Kunze, Linear Algebra, Prentice Hall.

Linear algebra is the computational core of every modern signal-processing, communication (MIMO, beamforming),

Course Code MA-L-02-C Credits 3
Structure (L-T-P-
Category BSC (Basic Science) 2-1-0-0
S)
Prerequisite Nil Laboratory No
Develops single- and multivariable calculus tools essential for modelling continuous systems, optimization, and
field theory in engineering.
Course Outcomes (COs)
On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to:
CO Statement
CO1 Find limits of functions graphically, numerically, and algebraically.
CO2 Apply continuity and differentiability to algebraic and transcendental functions.
CO3 Use partial derivatives, gradients, and Lagrange multipliers for optimization.
CO4 Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate definite integrals.
CO5 Evaluate multiple integrals to solve area, volume, and real-world problems.
Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules)
Mod. Content Hours
Single-Variable Calculus Review
M1 Limit, continuity and differentiability; indeterminate forms and L'Hospital rule; Mean 5
Value theorem; Maclaurin and Taylor series.
Functions of Several Variables
M2 Limits and continuity; partial derivatives and differentiability; linearization and 6
differentials; chain rule; gradient vector; tangent planes; directional derivatives.
Multivariable Optimization
M3 Extreme values and saddle points; Lagrange multipliers; Taylor's formula for several 5
variables; partial derivatives with constrained variables.
Double Integrals
M4 Double integrals; change of order of integration; area and volume by double integral; 6
double integrals in polar form.
Triple Integrals
M5 Triple integrals in rectangular, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates; substitutions in 6
multiple integrals; applications.
Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 28
Text Books
M. D. Weir, J. Hass, Thomas' Calculus, 12th ed., Pearson.
G. B. Thomas, R. L. Finney, Calculus and Analytic Geometry, 9th ed., Pearson.
Reference Books
Hughes-Hallett et al., Calculus: Single and Multivariable, 6th ed., Wiley.
J. Stewart, Multivariable Calculus, Hybrid Edition, Cengage.

recursion.
Pointers

allocation (malloc, calloc, realloc, free).
Structures, Unions & Files

binary files, file operations.

EC-L-01-C Digital Electronics using Verilog
Course Code EC-L-01-C Credits 3
Structure (L-T-P-
Category ESC (Engineering Science) 2-0-2-0
S)
Prerequisite Nil Laboratory Mandatory (2 Hours)
Introduces digital logic design and hardware description using Verilog HDL, forming the gateway to VLSI,
FPGA, and embedded design.
Course Outcomes (COs)
On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to:
CO Statement
CO1 Understand number systems, logic gates, Boolean simplification, and flip-flops.
CO2 Design basic digital systems using standard ICs and Verilog.
CO3 Analyse and design combinational circuits.
CO4 Analyse and design sequential circuits including counters and FSMs.
CO5 Implement and simulate digital designs in Verilog HDL.
Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules)
Mod. Content Hours
Number Systems & Boolean Algebra
M1 Number systems and conversions; logic gates and truth tables; Boolean algebra; K- 5
maps; NAND/NOR implementations; tabular (Quine-McCluskey) simplification.
Combinational Design - Arithmetic
M2 Design procedure; half/full adder and subtractor; 4-bit ripple-carry adder; carry-look- 6
ahead adder; BCD arithmetic.
Combinational Design - MSI
M3 Decoders, encoders, multiplexers, de-multiplexers, magnitude comparators; 5
implementing logic with MUX/decoders.
Sequential Circuits
M4 Latches and flip-flops; FF conversions; serial and parallel shift registers; synchronous 6
and asynchronous counter design.
FSM & Verilog HDL
M5 Mealy and Moore machines; state diagrams and tables; Verilog modelling styles (gate, 6
dataflow, behavioral); test benches and simulation.
Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 28

R. P. Jain, Modern Digital Electronics, 3rd ed., Tata McGraw-Hill, 2003.

2013.

Course Outcomes (COs)
On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to:
CO Statement
CO1 Classify continuous and discrete signals by their properties.
CO2 Classify systems based on their properties.
CO3 Analyse continuous-time signals and systems with appropriate tools.
CO4 Analyse sampling and discrete-time signals.
CO5 Determine Fourier transforms for continuous- and discrete-time signals.

Mod. Content Hours
Signals & Systems Basics
M1 Classification of signals; signal operations (scaling, shifting, inversion); signal properties; 6
elementary signals; classification and properties of systems.
LTI Systems & Convolution
Continuous-time LTI and discrete-time LSI systems; impulse and step response;
M2 6
convolution; system representation by differential/difference equations; eigenfunctions;
frequency response.
Fourier Analysis
M3 Fourier series of CT and DT signals; continuous-time Fourier transform and properties; 6
Parseval's relation; time-bandwidth product.
DTFT, DFT & Sampling
M4 Discrete-time Fourier transform and properties; relations among Fourier representations; 5
DFT; sampling theorem; aliasing; reconstruction (ideal interpolator, ZOH, FOH).
Transform-Domain Analysis
M5 Laplace/Z-transform: definition, region of convergence, properties; transform-domain 5
analysis of LTI/LSI systems; system function, poles and zeros; stability.

A deeper treatment of graph theory and its algorithms, central to networks, optimization, and many computing

Course Outcomes (COs)
On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to:
CO Statement
CO1 Apply graph terminology, representations, and properties.
CO2 Analyse connectivity, trees, and spanning structures.

CO5 Apply graph algorithms to real computing problems.

Mod. Content Hours
Graph Fundamentals
M1 Graphs, digraphs, and representations; degree sequences; isomorphism; walks, paths, 6
cycles; connectivity.
Trees & Connectivity
M2 Trees and their properties; spanning trees; minimum spanning trees; cut vertices and 7
edges; vertex/edge connectivity.
Matching & Colouring
M3 Bipartite graphs; matchings; Hall's theorem; vertex and edge colouring; chromatic 7
number; independent and dominating sets.
Planarity & Flows
M4 Planar graphs; Euler's formula; Kuratowski's theorem; network flows; max-flow min-cut 7
theorem.
Advanced Topics
M5 Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs; spectral graph theory (introduction); random graphs; 8
applications in social and computer networks.

computation.

Mod. Content Hours
Foundations of Finance — Overview of the financial system and institutions;
M1 time value of money; simple and compound interest; present value and future 5
value; inflation and purchasing power.
Personal Finance & Investment — Savings and budgeting; banking and
M2 digital payment systems; insurance basics; introduction to mutual funds and the 5
stock market; risk-return trade-off; retirement and tax planning basics.
Corporate Finance Basics — Reading financial statements (balance sheet,
M3 P&L, cash flow); key financial ratios; sources of business finance (equity, debt); 4
basics of capital budgeting.

About IIIT-NR
Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR) is
a premier state-funded institute established in 2015 under the International Institute of Information
Technology University Act, 2013 of the Government of Chhattisgarh. The institute is a joint initiative of the
Government of Chhattisgarh and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited, a Maharatna
Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Power, Government of India.
Incorporated as a state university and recognized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and
approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), IIIT-NR is committed to pursuing
excellence in higher education, research, and development in Information Technology (IT) and associated
disciplines. The institute firmly believes in knowledge dissemination and in imparting entrepreneurial skills
to its students, enabling them to address real-world problems with confidence and creativity.
The institute is housed on a fully residential, fifty-acre green campus in Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar) — India's
first planned green and smart city — approximately 23 km from Raipur and well connected by air, rail, and
road. The serene environment blends natural beauty with state-of-the-art infrastructure, creating an ideal
space for innovation and learning.
IIIT-NR offers undergraduate (B.Tech.), postgraduate (M.Tech.), and doctoral (Ph.D.) programmes in
Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), and Data
Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI). These credit-based programmes are designed to foster core
competence together with innovation and entrepreneurship, with a dynamic curriculum structure that keeps
pace with the changing needs of industry and academia.
Vision of the Institute
To be a globally recognized institution of excellence in information technology and allied disciplines,
nurturing innovators, entrepreneurs, and socially responsible technologists who contribute to national and
global development.
Mission of the Institute
• To impart high-quality, value-based, and outcome-oriented technical education.
• To foster state-of-the-art, interdisciplinary research and product development.
• To cultivate entrepreneurial mind-sets and industry-ready professional skills.
• To engage with society and industry for sustainable and inclusive growth.

B.Tech ECE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR
About the Department of ECE
The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) at IIIT-NR offers a four-year
Bachelor of Technology programme that provides a strong conceptual foundation in electronics,
communication, signal processing, and VLSI, complemented by intensive hands-on experience in
designing and building electronic hardware and embedded systems. The programme has been developed
in response to the evolving needs of industry, equipping students with advanced knowledge and skills for
the design of complex electronic and communication systems.
The department is taught by highly qualified and research-active faculty whose expertise spans wireless
and next-generation communications (5G/6G, OTFS, UAV networks), VLSI and microelectronics,
embedded and IoT systems, RF and microwave engineering, signal processing, control, and machine
learning for communications. Every semester integrates project work that combines coding and electronics
skills, supported by well-equipped laboratories and the active mentorship of research scholars.
Vision of the Department
To emerge as a centre of excellence in electronics and communication engineering education and research,
producing globally competent engineers and innovators capable of addressing the technological challenges
of a connected world.
Mission of the Department
To provide a rigorous, outcome-based foundation in electronics and communication engineering with
strong hands-on and design exposure.
To promote research, innovation, and entrepreneurship in emerging areas such as next-generation
wireless, VLSI, embedded systems, and intelligent electronics.
To inculcate professional ethics, lifelong learning, and social responsibility among students.
To build strong linkages with industry, research organizations, and the wider community for mutually
beneficial collaboration.
Programme Offered
B.Tech. in Electronics and Communication Engineering — 4 years / 8 semesters, 160 credits, with multiple
entry-exit options, multidisciplinary minors, an Honors track, and a strong project and internship component,
in line with NEP 2020 and the NBA outcome-based education framework.
Credit Structure and Break-up
The programme follows the NEP-based B.Tech. Common Format credit scheme, with a total programme
credit requirement of 160 credits distributed across Lecture (L), Tutorial (T), Practical (P), and Scholarly
Engagement Hours (S) components as defined below:
Credit Component (as per NEP-based
Definition / Contact-Hour Equivalence
B.Tech. Common Format)
L — Lecture 1 Credit = 1 hour / week
T — Tutorial 1 Credit = 1 hour / week
P — Practical 1 Credit = 2 hours / week
S — Scholarly Engagement Hours 0 Credit = 2 hours / week
Salient Features of the Curriculum
• Choice-based credit system with Program Electives (Communications, Embedded Systems, VLSI
tracks), Open Electives, and Multidisciplinary Minors.

academics-btech_ece_syllabus_2025:p026.text:
B.Tech ECE Syllabus • Dr. SPM IIIT-NR
Detailed Course-wise Syllabus (Core Subjects)
This section presents the detailed Outcome-Based Education (OBE) syllabus for the core (compulsory) courses
of the programme, covering the Basic Science (BSC), Engineering Science (ESC), Programme Core (PCC), and
Programme Science (PSC) courses from Semester 1 to Semester 6. Each course is described using a uniform
OBE template comprising: course information, Course Outcomes (COs), a five-module detailed syllabus with
contact hours, text and reference books, industry relevance, Open Educational Resources (OERs) and open

M2 6

analysis of LTI/LSI systems; system function, poles and zeros; stability.

EC-L-23-C Testing and Verification of VLSI Circuits
Course Code EC-L-23-C Credits 2
Structure (L-T-P-
Category PCC (Programme Core) 1-0-2-0
S)
Prerequisite VLSI Design and IC Technology Laboratory Mandatory
Covers fault modelling, test generation, design-for-test, and functional verification methods essential to the
modern VLSI/SoC design flow.
Course Outcomes (COs)
On successful completion of this course, the student will be able to:
CO Statement
CO1 Explain fault models and the need for VLSI testing.
CO2 Generate test patterns for combinational and sequential circuits.
CO3 Apply design-for-testability (DFT) techniques.
CO4 Describe built-in self-test (BIST) and boundary-scan methods.
CO5 Apply functional-verification methodology to digital designs.
Detailed Syllabus (5 Modules)
Mod. Content Hours
Testing Fundamentals
M1 Need for testing; faults vs errors vs defects; fault models - stuck-at, bridging, delay; fault 5
coverage; yield.
Test Generation
M2 Fault simulation; combinational ATPG - D-algorithm, PODEM; sequential test 5
generation; testability measures (SCOAP).
Design for Testability
M3 Ad-hoc DFT; scan design; full and partial scan; test-point insertion; test-cost 5
considerations.
BIST & Boundary Scan
M4 Built-in self-test architectures; LFSR-based pattern generation and signature analysis; 5
boundary scan (JTAG / IEEE 1149.1).
Verification Methodology
M5 Simulation-based verification; testbenches; assertions; code/functional coverage; 4
introduction to UVM concepts.
Total Contact Hours (Lecture) 24
Text Books
M. Bushnell, V. Agrawal, Essentials of Electronic Testing for Digital, Memory and Mixed-Signal VLSI
Circuits, Springer.
M. Abramovici, M. Breuer, A. Friedman, Digital Systems Testing and Testable Design, Wiley-IEEE.
Reference Books
L.-T. Wang, C.-W. Wu, X. Wen, VLSI Test Principles and Architectures, Morgan Kaufmann.
C. Spear, G. Tumbush, SystemVerilog for Verification, Springer.

Industry Relevance
Test and verification engineers are critical in every semiconductor company, as silicon cannot ship without thorough
DFT and verification. Scan, BIST, ATPG, and verification skills map directly to DFT and design-verification (DV) roles
in ASIC/SoC teams.

• EDA Playground (SystemVerilog/UVM) — https://www.edaplayground.com/

Stuck-at fault simulation on a combinational circuit.
ATPG pattern generation exercise.
Scan-chain insertion and verification.
LFSR-based BIST pattern generation.
Testbench with assertions and coverage using cocotb.

Introduces students to the fundamental concepts of personal and corporate finance, building the financial

CO Statement
Explain core financial concepts, including the time value of money and interest
CO1
computation.

Foundations of Finance — Overview of the financial system and institutions;
M1 time value of money; simple and compound interest; present value and future 5
value; inflation and purchasing power.
Personal Finance & Investment — Savings and budgeting; banking and
M2 digital payment systems; insurance basics; introduction to mutual funds and the 5
stock market; risk-return trade-off; retirement and tax planning basics.
Corporate Finance Basics — Reading financial statements (balance sheet,
M3 P&L, cash flow); key financial ratios; sources of business finance (equity, debt); 4
basics of capital budgeting.

Financial literacy is essential for engineers managing project budgets, evaluating ESOPs/stock

Rubric Frameworks for Evaluation of Community Engagement Activities (NSS/ISR) / Extra and Co-
Curricular Activities
Semester V
A. NSS (Hours of Service): NSS Coordinator will be responsible for providing the grade
Grade A+ A B+ B C+ C F
Hours of ≥ 240 200-239 180-199 140-179 100-139 60-99 <60
service
B. ISR (30 Activities in Two years): ISR Coordinator will be responsible for providing the grade
Grade A+ A B+ B C+ C F
Present ≥ 90% 80%- 70%- 60%- 50%- 40%- <40%
in % of 89% 79% 69% 59% 49%
activities
a. Students can attend any one activity to earn the grade.
b. If a student wants to increase their grade, they need to participate in another activity also.
Then the final grade will be decided by combining the grades of the two activities (NSS
and ISR). For example, If a student scores an A in NSS and a C in ISR, his final grade will
be A+. In general, students will be given one grade above the maximum grade of two
activities, provided both grades are C and above.
c. For an F grade, the student has to do all ISR activities in the next semester.
Semester VI
Co-curricular & Extra-curricular Activities
Students' participation in the institute activities up to IV sem
a. Different clubs: technical and non-technical clubs; the coordinator of clubs will provide
the names of students with attendance in the number of sessions and achievements
b. Sports activities: participation in institute sports activities and sports competition: The SAC
president will be responsible for providing the participant's name
c. Attend IEEE activities and institute talk: The IEEE Coordinator will be responsible for
providing the name
d. Volunteers in different technical and non-technical events. The faculty coordinator of
particular activities will be responsible for providing the participant's name.
All activities will have equal weightage.

Course Title Linear Algebra & Matrix Analysis Course Code MA01

& MGMT. T-P-S)
Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory

Course Outcomes
At the end of the course, students should be able to:
Solve systems of linear equations using multiple methods, including Gaussian elimination and
matrix inversion.
Carry out matrix operations, including inverses and determinants.
Determine eigenvalues and eigenvectors and solve eigenvalue problems.
Apply principles of matrix algebra to linear transformations.
Demonstrate understanding of inner products and associated norms.

System of linear equations, Inverse and rank of a matrix by using elementary transformations,
Properties of determinants
Vector space over real and complex fields, Linear dependence, independence and spanning set,
Linear transformation and its matrix, Change of basis, Eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
Diagonalization of matrices.
Inner product spaces, Gram-Schmidt orthonormalization, Singular Value Decomposition (SVD).

Course Title Calculus Course Code MA02
Department CSE/ECE/DSAI/SCI. & Credits, Structure ( L-T- 3, (2-1-0-0)
MATHS/HUMANITIES & MGMT. P-S)
Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory
Prerequisite NA Laboratory No
Course Outcomes
At the end of the course, students should be able to:
Find limits of functions (graphically, numerically and algebraically)
Analyse and apply the notions of continuity and differentiability to algebraic and
transcendental functions.
Determine derivatives using implicit differentiation and use to study characteristics of a curve.
Apply the Fundamental theorem of calculus to evaluate definite integrals.
Use differentiation and integration to solve real world problems such as rate of change,
optimization, and area problems.
Contents:
Review of single variable calculus: Review of Limit, continuity and differentiability of single variable
functions, Indeterminate forms and L’Hospital rule, Mean Value theorem, Maclaurin and Taylor
series expansions of functions of one variable.
Functions of Several variables: Functions of several variables, Limits and continuity, Partial
derivatives and differentiability, Linearization and differentials, Chain rule, Gradient vector, Tangent
planes, Directional derivatives, Extreme values and saddle points, Lagrange multipliers, Taylor’s
formula, Partial derivatives with constrained variables.
Multiple integral: Multiple integral, Double integrals, Change of order of integration, Area and
volume by double integral, Double integrals in polar form, Triple integrals in rectangular
coordinates, Triple integrals in cylindrical and spherical coordinates, Substitutions in multiple
integrals.
Text Books
M. D. Weir and J. Hass, Thomas’ Calculus, 12 th edition, Pearson.
G. B. Thomas and R. L. Finney, Calculus and Analytic Geometry, 9th Ed, Pearson.
Huges-Hallett et al, Calculus: Single and Multivariable, 6 th edition, John-Wiley & Sons (USA).
J. Stewart, Multivariable Calculus, Hybrid Edition.

IT Workshop: Full Stack Prototyping with Course Code SK01
Course Title
AI Support
Department CSE/ECE/DSAI/SCI. & MATHS/HUMANITIES Credits, Structure ( L- 2, (1-0-2-2)
& MGMT. T-P-[C])
Offered for All Programs Type Compulsory
Prerequisite NA Laboratory Choice Mandatory
Course Description: This hands-on workshop enables students to design, develop, and deploy end-to-end functional
prototypes for web and mobile applications, leveraging AI-powered tools for faster development. The course blends
Full Stack development (front-end, back-end, and database) with AI-assisted features such as code generation, UI
design, data handling, and intelligent services.
Course Outcomes (COs): On successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
 CO1: Apply fundamental concepts of full stack development (frontend, backend, database, APIs) to
design functional prototypes.
 CO2: Use AI-assisted tools to accelerate coding, interface design, and backend logic development.
 CO3: Integrate AI/ML services (e.g., Chatbots, Recommendation Engines, Vision APIs) into full stack
prototypes.
 CO4: Deploy prototypes to cloud platforms for public access.
 CO5: Collaborate effectively in teams, managing workflows using modern DevOps tools and agile
principles.
Mapping to Graduate Attributes: Engineering knowledge, Problem Analysis, Design/Development, Modern Tool
Usage, Ethics, Communication, and Project Management.
Course Contents:
Module 1 – Introduction & Tools Setup (Week 1) - Full Stack architecture overview (Client–Server–Database), AI-
powered development tools: GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Cursor, Replit, etc., Setting up environment: Node.js,
Python/Flask/Django, React/Vue, VS Code, Git/GitHub
Module 2 – Frontend Development with AI Assistance (Weeks 2–3) - HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript ES6+ basics
(AI-assisted code snippets), Component-based UI design using React/Vue, Responsive design frameworks
(Bootstrap/Tailwind CSS), AI-assisted prototyping for UI/UX
Module 3 – Backend Development & APIs (Weeks 4–5) - REST API concepts and design, Backend frameworks:
Express.js / Flask / Django, AI-assisted code scaffolding for CRUD operations, Authentication & authorization basics
Module 4 – Databases & Integration (Week 6) - SQL (MySQL/PostgreSQL) and NoSQL (MongoDB), AI-assisted
query generation and optimization, ORM integration (SQLAlchemy, Mongoose)
Module 5 – AI/ML Service Integration (Weeks 7–8) - Integrating OpenAI, Hugging Face, or Google Cloud AI APIs,
Adding chatbots, summarizers, sentiment analysis, or computer vision to prototypes, Data preprocessing using AI
tools
Module 6 – Deployment & DevOps Basics (Week 9) - Deploying applications using Vercel, Netlify, or Heroku,
Containerization with Docker (optional), AI-assisted CI/CD setup
Module 7 – Project Sprint & Demo Day (Weeks 10–12) - Agile project management tools, (Trello/Jira), Team sprints
with AI-assisted task completion, Final demo and peer evaluation
Course Projects (Examples): Students will work in teams to develop one full stack prototype with AI-assisted
features. Possible project ideas include:
AI-Powered Resume Builder – Generates resumes using user input, with real-time formatting and
download options.
E-Commerce Portal with AI Recommendations – AI-based product suggestions and chatbot support.
Smart Student Portal – With AI-assisted assignment summaries and automated FAQs.
Travel Itinerary Planner – AI-generated itineraries based on preferences, with map integration.
Healthcare Symptom Checker – Uses NLP models to provide probable condition information.

Text Books:
Srinivasa K G, et al., AI-Assisted Programming for Web and Machine Learning, BPB Publishers, 2025.
Bates, B., & Downey, C., Programming with AI Tools: A Developer’s Guide, Manning Publications.
References:
 OpenAI API Documentation – https://platform.openai.com/docs
 Hugging Face API Documentation – https://huggingface.co/docs
 Mozilla Developer Network (MDN) – https://developer.mozilla.org/
 Docker Documentation – https://docs.docker.com/
 Tailwind CSS Docs – https://tailwindcss.com/docs
 GitHub Copilot Guide – https://docs.github.com/copilot

Course Outcomes
At the end of the course, students should be able to:
Use with the language of basic quantum mechanics and formalism.
carry out calculations of atoms and molecules and describe quantum phenomenon within the
electron physics from quantum mechanical relations.
carry out spectroscopic studies of different subjects and interpret the results in quantized

report on applications of quantum physics in nature, technical developments and society.

Basics of Quantum Mechanics: Basic principles of quantum mechanics, wave function and the
uncertainty principle, probability wave amplitude, probability density, wave equation and

eigenstates and eigenvalues of angular momentum, central potential, solutions of Schrodinger
equation in a central potential and applications (Hydrogen-like atom).
Dirac’s bra and ket algebra: Introduction, bra and ket notation, angular momenta, Clebsch-Gordon
coefficients, spin-orbit interaction and applications. Hilbert space and concept of Qubits.

Course Title Signals and Systems Course Code ECE02

Course Outcomes
At the end of the course, students should be able to:
Understand different types of signals-continuous and discrete, odd and even, periodic and
aperiodic etc.
Classify systems based on their properties
Analyse continuous time signals and systems by using appropriate mathematical tools
Analyse sampling process and sampling of discrete time signals.
Determine Fourier transforms for continuous-time and discrete-time signals
Contents:
Signals: classification of signals; signal operations: scaling, shifting and inversion; signal properties;
elementary signals.
Systems: classification of systems; system properties; continuous-time linear time invariant (LTI)
and discrete-time linear shift invariant (LSI) systems: impulse response and step response; response
to an arbitrary input: convolution; system representation using differential and difference
equations; Eigen functions of LTI systems, frequency response and its relation to the impulse
response.
Fourier series representation of continuous-time and discrete-time signals, continuous-time Fourier
transform and its properties; Parseval’s relation, time-bandwidth product; discrete-time Fourier
transform and its properties; relations among various Fourier representations, Time and Frequency
characterization of Signals and Systems, DFT.
Sampling theorem; aliasing; signal reconstruction: ideal interpolator, zero-order hold, first-order
hold.
Definition, region of convergence, properties; transform-domain analysis of LTI/LSI systems, system
function: poles and zeros; stability.

Course Outcomes At the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Understand different types of signals-continuous and discrete, odd and even, periodic and aperiodic etc. 2. Classify systems based on their properties 3. Analyse continuous time signals and systems by using appropriate mathematical tools 4. Analyse sampling process and sampling of discrete time signals. 5. Determine Fourier transforms for continuous-time and discrete-time signals Contents: Signals: classification of signals; signal operations: scaling, shifting and inversion; signal properties; elementary signals. Systems: classification of systems; system properties; continuous-time linear time invariant (LTI) and discrete-time linear shift invariant (LSI) systems: impulse response and step response; response to an arbitrary input: convolution; system representation using differential and difference equations; Eigen functions of LTI systems, frequency response and its relation to the impulse response. Fourier series representation of continuous-time and discrete-time signals, continuous-time Fourier transform and its properties; Parseval’s relation, time-bandwidth product; discrete-time Fourier transform and its properties; relations among various Fourier representations, Time and Frequency characterization of Signals and Systems, DFT. Sampling theorem; aliasing; signal reconstruction: ideal interpolator, zero-order hold, first-order hold. Definition, region of convergence, properties; transform-domain analysis of LTI/LSI systems, system function: poles and zeros; stability. Text Books 1. A.V. Oppenheim, A.S. Willsky and H.S. Fannin, "Signals and Systems - Continuous and Discrete", 4/e, Prentice Hall, 1998. | | | | |

Course Objectives:

manner.

 Encourage curiosity and self-learning through open platforms like Kaggle, AIcrowd, and Google Colab.

CO2: Describe fundamental rights, duties, and directive principles. CO3: Identify the structure and functioning of the Union, State, and Local Governments. Dipanjan Sar (Electronics and Communication Engineering)
Dipanjan Sar is a dedicated researcher specializing in wireless communication, AI/ML, Internet of Vehicles (IoV) communication, and waveform design. He is currently pursuing his Ph.D. in Electronics and Communication Engineering at IIIT Naya Raipur, alongside working as a Senior Research Fellow (SRF) in a National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) funded project.

Dipanjan has also contributed significantly to academia, having over three years of teaching experience at Techno India Banipur (WB) and Chaibasa Engineering College (Jharkhand). His expertise lies in bridging the gap between theoretical research and practical applications, driving innovation in wireless communication and intelligent vehicular networks.

Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute
of Information Technology, Naya Raipur
I. About IIIT Naya Raipur
Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee IIIT-Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR), established by
the International Institute of Information Technology University Act, 2013
of the Government of Chhattisgarh, is a joint initiative of the Chhattisgarh
State Government and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC). The
institute is committed to pursuing excellence in higher education, research,
and development in information technology (IT) and other associated
disciplines. IIIT-NR firmly believes in bestowing knowledge dissemination
and imparting entrepreneurial skills to the students to enable them to
address real-world problems. To empower this vision, IIIT-NR provides
state-of-the-art research and education facilities and nurtures a campus
culture that fosters high energy and enthusiasm in every individual, clubbed
with the highest standard of professionalism.
Facilities:
The 50 acres of the lush green campus of IIIT-NR is enabled with Wi-Fi
connectivity and has excellent amenities for sports and other recreational
activities. The modern architecture of the buildings and the serene
environment of the campus foster an ambience for the students to engage in
creativity and innovation.
The institute has two state-of-the-art virtual classrooms of 120 capacity each
quipped with the latest video conferencing systems. The classrooms and laboratories
are equipped with state-of-the-art tools for teaching and learning. Some important
laboratories are the 3D Printing & Fabrication Lab, 5G Lab, Antenna and Microwave
Circuit Design Lab, Big Data Computing Lab, VLSI & Embedded Lab, Artificial
Intelligence & Deep Learning Lab, Communication Lab, Data Science Lab, IoT &
Sensor Lab, Robotics Lab, etc.
IIIT-NR Guest House 20 Rooms air-
conditioned, furnished and provided
with attached bathrooms with dining
facilities. Parents or guardians of the
students or experts can stay with the
approval of the competent authority.
Hostel Facilities::
IIIT-NR has four hostels for boys and three for
girls. Students can access campus networks and
computing facilities from their hostel rooms
through high-speed WiFi/LAN. All students are
required to stay in a hostel.
Canteen Facilities:
The institute has separate dining facilities for boys and girls in
their hostels. Additionally, it has a centralised canteen that serves
snacks, vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, general fast food, juice, and milk
products. The institute’s mess serves both vegetarian and non-vegetarian food. The
mess is managed by a committee comprising students, staff, and faculty.
Sports Facilities:
Every hostel has a separate sports facility for indoor games, including table tennis
and badminton. A multi purpose indoor hall with four badminton courts cum a
basket ball court, one out door basketball court, two volleyball courts and one
football cum cricket ground are available. Indoor game facilities are available in
each hostel apart from the SAC (Student Activities Centre).
Gym:
Open-air Gym facilities with modern equipment are available separately for boys
and girls. A centralised indoor Gym facility is also available at SAC.
Auditorium
The institute has a centrally air-
conditioned auditorium with an
800-seat capacity for organising
large technical and cultural
events.
Amphitheatres:
The institute has two open-air
theatres with a capacity of 1500
and 1000 for its cultural activities.

II. Academic Programs
IIIT-NR currently runs three undergraduate programs: B. Tech. in Computer
Science & Engineering (CSE), B. Tech. in Electronics & Communication
Engineering (ECE) and B. Tech. in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence
(DSAI). These credit-based programs are designed to foster core skills with
innovation and entrepreneurship skills among students. The dynamic
structure of the curriculum orchestrates with the changing needs of industry
and academia. IIIT-NR also runs postgraduate and doctoral programs as
mentioned in the table below:

More information on Academics and the Curriculum is available at
https://www.iiitnr.ac.in/ content/programs
III. Admission to B.Tech. Programs:
Admission to the B.Tech. programmes at IIIT Naya Raipur is governed solely by
the JEE (Main) 2026 rank. There are 90 seats available in each CSE, ECE, and
DSAI. Additionally there are some female only supernumerary seats and 1
Kashmiri Migrant seat in each branch. Eligible candidates may apply under the
following categories:
All India Quota Chhattisgarh Quota NTPC Quota
Eligibility Criteria, Seats and Reservation
All India Quota: 35% of seats, amounting to 95 seats (32 in CSE, 32 in ECE
and 31 in DSAI) are in this category. Additionally there are 24 female only
supernumerary seats (8 in each branch), reserved only for female candidates.
Candidates who completed their school education in any part of India can apply
under this category. These seats will be filled through JoSAA/CSAB 2026
counselling (visit https://josaa.nic.in). So their eligibility will be as per the
business rules of JoSAA 2026. All reservations will be as per the
Government of India norms.
NTPC Quota: 15% of seats, amounting to 40 seats (16 in CSE, 17 in ECE and 17
in DSAI) are in this category. Additionally there are 10 female only
supernumerary seats (3 in CSE, 3 in DSAI, 4 in ECE ), reserved only for female
candidates. Candidates employed with NTPC or their wards who completed their
school education in any part of India can apply under this category. Their
eligibility will be as per the business rules of JoSAA/CSAB 2026. All
reservations will be as per the Government of India norms. These seats
will be filled through the IIIT-NR online counselling process (visit
https://www.iiitnr.ac.in/content/b-tech-admission-2026) Candidates seeking
admission under NTPC quota seats shall submit a certificate in the prescribed
format (Annexure I) from the Nodal Authority of NTPC, certifying that the
candidate is eligible to apply for the NTPC quota.
The candidates applying for OBC-NCL under All India and NTPC quota must
submit the OBC-NCL certificate in the format (Annexure II) provided by the JoSAA
Other formats are not acceptable.
Chhattisgarh Quota: 50% of seats amount to 135 seats (45 in CSE, 45 in ECE
and 45 in DSAI) in this category. All the reservations under this quota will be as
per the norms of the Govt. of Chhattisgarh. These seats will be filled through
the IIIT-NR online counselling process (visit https://www.iiitnr.ac.in/
content/b-tech-admission-2026) The following are the eligibility criteria for
admission under this quota:

Candidates must pass the 10th and 12th standard examinations from the
schools in the State of Chhattisgarh only.
2.Candidates must have scored 50% aggregate marks in Chemistry, Physics and
Mathematics (45% for SC/ST/OBC-NCL/PwD candidates) in their 12th
standard examination.
3.Candidates’ date of birth must be on or after October 01, 2000. For the
candidates belonging to SC, ST, OBC-NCL and PwD, the upper age limit is
relaxable by three years, i.e. SC, ST, OBC-NCL, and PwD candidates’ date of
birth must be on or after October 01, 1997. Only the date of birth recorded by
the Secondary Education Board will be considered.
4.Candidates who passed their 12th standard examination or any other
qualifying examination in 2024, 2025 or 2026 shall be eligible. The
candidates who appeared in the 12th standard or equivalent qualifying
examinations in 2023, did not pass in 2023, but passed in 2024 are not
eligible.
5.Candidates seeking admission under reserved categories (SC/ ST/ OBC -
NCL) have to mandatorily submit their caste/category certificate issued by a
competent authority of Govt. of Chhattisgarh only in their name at the
time of application.
6.OBC-NCL candidates are required to produce an OBC-NCL certificate issued,
by the competent authorities, on or after 1st April 2026.
As per Govt. of Chhattisgarh norms, in addition to the vertical reservations
(SC/ST/OBC NCL), the following horzental reservations under the above
verticals:
Women – 30%
Children of Ex-Servicemen – 5%
Children or Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters – 3%
Persons with Disabilities – 5%
^ 2% of seats are reserved for the candidates of the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal
Group (PVTP) from the seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes (ST).
8.The wards/grandchildren of Freedom Fighters (FF) shall have to submit a
certificate (Annexure III) issued by the competent authorities that his/her
parent/grandparent is a freedom fighter.
9.The wards of Ex‐servicemen shall have to submit a certificate (Annexure IV)
issued by the Army Commanding Officer or Zila Sainik Welfare Officers.
10.For Persons with Disabilities (PwD), the following certificates are required
to be submitted:
i. Certificate issued by District Medical Board certifying disability
ii. Certificate from Superintendent, Government of India, and Ministry of
Labour certifying that candidate is eligible to study for the subject applied.
A caste/category certificate issued in the name of either of the parents
(Mother/ Father) is unacceptable.
Forwards of Kashmiri Migrants, a certificate from the competent authority (Sub‐
Divisional Officer ‐ Revenue) is required.
IV Application Procedure and Fee
Candidates desirous of seeking admission to IIIT-NR under the CG quota and/or
NTPC quota must apply through the institute’s online portal
(https://www.iiitnr.ac.in/content/b-tech-admission-2026). Offline applications
or applications via email will not be considered.
Application & Counselling Process: Candidates applying for admissions
shall be required to remit a non-refundable application fee of Rs. 500/- online.
Based on the online applications received and their respective JEE (Main) 2026
rank, merit lists will be published for each category. The entire admission
process will strictly be conducted online as per the announced schedule. Any
changes in the deadlines or alterations in the process will be duly communicated
on our website. Any physical solicitation concerning the Admission Process will

IIIT Naya Raipur invites applications to full time M.Tech. programs in Computer Science & Engineering and Electronics & Communication Engineering for the year 2026-2027. All India Quota (35% seats amounting to 14(+2 EWS) seats: 07+1 in CSE and 07+1 in ECE): Applicants who completed their school education from any part of India belong to this category. NTPC Quota (15% seats amounting to 06 seats: 03 in CSE and 03 in ECE): Applicants employed with NTPC or their wards who have completed their school education from any part of India belong to this category. Reservation as per GOI Norms

The CM IT Fellowship Program aims to empower and train the local young professionals in the field of Software-Driven Analysis. The programme is exclusively for Chhattisgarh-domiciled candidates, ensuring local talent is nurtured for the state’s development. The program is structured in collaboration with multiple stakeholders, including
∙ Chhattisgarh Infotech Promotion Society (CHiPS)
∙ IIIT Naya Raipur
∙ Various Government departments of Chhattisgarh.
The MTech program in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (DSAI) is designed to provide participants with deep technical expertise while involving them in meaningful governance projects, enhancing their skills for both personal and societal growth.
Key features of the program:
Fellowship: Rs 50000 per month in both 1st and 2nd years Sponsored by Govt. of Chhattisgarh.
Tuition Fee: Up to 2 lakhs is Sponsored by the Govt. of Chhattisgarh.
Laptop/Desktop will be provided with all the necessary software at free of cost by the Govt. of Chhattisgarh subject to the availability and submission of necessary caution deposits.
Blended Learning Approach (in-person classes + Govt Dept engagement).
Unparalleled Exposure: The MTech program integrates (a) classroom learning at IIIT-Naya Raipur, and (b) Real-world governance experience in key administrative offices such as State Departments.
Career Advantage : Graduates will develop proficiency in emerging technologies like Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, equipping them to address challenges within the public sector. This aligns with the growing trend of applying AI in government to enhance efficiency and service delivery.
Lodging and Boarding: The admitted candidates will be provided lodging and boarding in the hostels as per the rules of IIIT NR on the payment basis during their stay IIIT NR for academic engagement.
Mode of Learning
Blended learning approach (in-person classes + Government Department engagement). In government Engagement, Fellows would get a chance to work in a Governance project envisaging practical experience.
Program Eligibility and Admission Criteria:
A candidate seeking admission into CM IT Fellowship MTech in DSAI has to satisfy the following requirements:
Nationality: The candidate must be a citizen of India and Domicile of Chhattisgarh.
Age Limit – up to 30 years^ as of the application deadline. Age relaxations are as per Chhattisgarh Govt. reservation rules.
Any graduate or post graduate student with GATE (in CS/DSAI) qualified and a minimum CPI# of 6.5 or 60% or First Class in the qualifying degree (5% marks or 0.5 CPI is relaxed for SC/ST/PwD Candidates).
Reservation Policy:
Reservation is applicable as per the Chhattisgarh State Reservation Policy.
Admission and selection process:
Admission process: Candidates desirous of seeking admission in M.Tech. (DSAI) CM IT Fellowship Programs must apply through the IIIT NR Admission portal https://erp.iiitnr.edu.in/OnlineApplicationRegistrationAndLogin.action. Each applicant has to pay Rs. 500/-. Offline applications or applications via email will not be considered.
