Responsibility (ISR) Club of IIIT-NR work with a vision to create
community awareness among the students and to develop a sense
of social and civic responsibility among themselves. It encourages
students to utilize their knowledge in generating practical solutions
to individual and community problems with the motto of ‘Not Me
But You’. These clubs have undertaken many initiatives towards
conserving the environment, educating the underprivileged
sections of society, and observing cleanliness and hygiene in the
locality.

Annual Report 2022-23
Activities of Students’ Clubs under SAC
As explained earlier, SAC organises various activities for overall growth and development of
students of IIIT-NR. Accordingly, these activities are primarily in the following areas:-
 Sharpening technical skill-sets of students
 Fostering soft-skills and leadership qualities
 Promoting art and culture
 Sports and games
 Social service and upliftment
Details of some of the noteworthy and useful activities organised by the SAC in the above-
mentioned areas in the year 2022-23 are as follows.
Technical Skills Activities
Blockchain Master Class
Cyber Security Club of IIIT-NR, Cipher Cell, conducted a series of sessions ‘Blockchain Master
Class’, to create interest, foster Blockchain Technology development skills and provide a
learning opportunity for enthusiastic students in Blockchain. The sessions were conducted on
April 01, April, 08 and April 29, 2022.
Bit to Byte
The coding club of IIIT-NR, The Society of Coders (TSoC), organized a series of coding related
competitions, ‘Bit to Byte’, on April 09-10, 2022. The competitions covered various aspects of
an interview, from coding round to Computer Science Fundamentals round. The event
mimicked the corporate environment, and teamwork was essential to compete in the event. The
competition events included Competitive Programming contest (Based on ICPC format),
Coding Speed Run, Machine Learning Contest, Aptitude and Math Contest, Computer Science
Fundamentals, English, Coding for Girls, etc. Teams for the events were created through an
IPL-like auction. The events were conducted in Codeforces, Vjudge and Kaggle platforms.
Internal Smart India Hackathon - SIH 2022
AIML Club of IIIT-NR organized an internal Smart
India Hackathon – SIH 2022, on April 20, 2022.
The event aimed to foster development skills in the
students, and provide a learning opportunity for
enthusiastic students of AIML. The problem
statements were selected based on real-life
problems and aimed at improving the basic
understanding and problem solving skills of
students.

event aimed to foster development skills in the students and provide a learning opportunity for

using basic Computer Vision techniques. All the groups completed the task with better
understanding of Python and OpenCV.

workshop on ‘Working of Robots’ on September 17,
The workshop provided introduction to robots
and their working with demonstration of two robots
Meshmerize and Cozmo Clench. Robonite as a CS-
STEAM Education platform brings forth an activity
based hands-on learning system that can be applied to
involve students in designing and building exciting robots, using LEGO Mind storm robotics
kits; thereby enhancing their mathematical reasoning and logical skills.
Machine Learning Mania-2k22
AIML Club of IIIT-NR organized a Hackathon ‘Machine Learning Mania-2k22’ from May 14-
16, 2022. The event aimed to foster development skills in the students and provide a learning
opportunity for enthusiastic students of AIML. During the contest, participants developed a
Machine Learning model to predict house prices. The event improved the students’
understanding and problem-solving skills in Keras, Python, Numpy, Pandas, Seaborn and
Matplotlib.
Machine Learning Project ‘Cognitio’
AIML Club of IIIT-NR organized a machine learning project
building event ‘Cognito’, from June 15, 2022 to July 30, 2022. The
unique initiative gave students an opportunity to make exciting
projects for solving real-world problems, under the direct guidance
of AIML team members. Candidates had to complete their allotted
projects within the given time.
The NFT Drop
The cybersecurity cell of IIIT-NR, CipherCell and the cultural club
of IIIT-NR Indradhanush, jointly organized a NFT (Non-Fungible
Tokens) design competition ‘The NFT Drop’ from August 16-23,

general-annual_report_2022_2023:p080.text:
The motive of the event was to enhance the designing skills
of students, giving them a platform to display their NFTs and to give
them an opportunity to delve deeper into the realm of NFTs. NFTs
are cryptographic assets on a Blockchain with unique identification
codes and metadata that distinguish them from each other and
cannot be replicated. NFTs can represent real-world items like artwork and real estate.

general-annual_report_2022_2023:p083.text:
Annual Report 2022-23
IDEACRYPT
The Electronics Club of IIIT-NR ComEt organized an event
‘Ideacrypt’ on September 18, 2022 to provide a platform for
students to present their innovative ideas for solving
challenging problems through technological means.
Students were given problem statements related to health,
sports and fitness, agriculture, smart automation, smart
education, and clean and green energy. Their job was to pitch
an idea/ concept to solve that problem by a hardware solution
and to present their solution (with concept level diagram/
architecture), advantages/ disadvantages, implementation, etc.
Code Nubs 3.0
The coding club of IIIT-NR, The Society of Coders (TSoC),
organized ‘Code Nubs 3.0’, on January 08, 2023, for the freshers to
help them begin their journey in competitive programming. The
competition was held in Codeforces platform.
Disrupt 3.0
Entrepreneurship Cell (E-Cell) of IIIT-NR hosted ‘Disrupt 3.0’ on
January 18, 2023. Participating team had to pitch their ideas on the
spot on how to market and sell a product made from an object that
was given to their team. To keep the competition challenging for
participants, business models were assigned to the teams during the
event and they were judged based on the innovation and feasibility
of their idea, as well as the pitching abilities of the speakers.
DesCode
The coding club of IIIT-NR The Society of Coders (TSoC)
organized a coding competition ‘DesCode’ on February 05, 2023,
to help the students improve their competitive programming skills.
The contest had three Data Structure and Algorithm (DSA)
problems and participants were given two hours to solve the
problem.
Kaggle Competition
The AIML club of IIIT-NR organized Kaggle Competition
‘ML Mania 2023’ on February 07, 2023, to introduce the
Batch 2022 students to Kaggle competitions and improve
their skills in the same to foster a competitive spirit. A
session was arranged for the students to make them familiar
with Kaggle and basic ML algorithms.
72 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍
Annual Report 2022-23
The Big Bull: A Virtual Stock Market Challenge
E-Cell of IIIT-Naya Raipur organized a virtual stock market
simulation challenge ‘The Big Bull’, from February 06-10, 2023,
to enable the participating students to get a head-start to their stock
market journey.
Machine Learning Hackathon
AIML club of IIIT-NR organized ‘ML Hackathon’ on March 18, 2023. The event's objective
was to familiarize the first-year students with Kaggle and basic ML algorithms. This
competition was a continuation of the last session arranged, which primarily focused on the
basics of Data Analysis using Pandas. It ended with a Code-along session to develop a basic
Linear Regression model and submit the output to the competition.
CodeRush Challenge 2023
The coding club of IIIT-NR, The Society of Coders (TSoC), organized a coding competition
‘CodeRush Challenge 2023’, in collaboration with Algo University, on March 22-23, 2023. On
the first day of the event, a webinar was organized, in which Mr. Swapnil Daga (Co-Founder of
Algo University), shared the placement preparation roadmap and tips. He shared his insights on
what makes a project presentable. The programming competition took place on the second day.
Soft-skills and Leadership Activities
Word War Edition 1.0
The Debating Society of IIIT-NR, Take-da-bait,
organized an event “Word War Edition 1.0”, on
April 02, 2022. The debate was held in standard
oxford template. The aim of the competition was to
give the students an experience of speaking in a
formal debate setup and to make them familiar with
oxford format. The competition also trained the
students to think creatively and generate relevant
arguments and helped them to develop persuasive
responses to simple questions.
֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 73

general-annual_report_2022_2023:p084.text:
Annual Report 2022-23
Group Discussion on India’s Journey from Partition to Present
The Model United Nations club of IIIT-NR conducted a group discussion on ‘What If - India’s
Journey from Partition to Present’ on September 09,
The objective of the event was to provide a
platform to students to share their opinions on some
of the most important events that have defined India’s
journey since independence. This event proved to be
helpful in encouraging students to learn about the
major political, social and economic events of our
post-independence history. A platform for group
discussion also helped students to develop leadership
and public speaking skills.
Model United Nations (MUN) Conference
The Model United Nations (MUN) Club of
IIIT-NR conducted a 2-day conference under
the two committees namely- All India Political
Parties Meet (AIPPM) and Disarmament and
International Security Committee (DISEC).
The AIPPM discussed on the topic
‘Safeguarding the Integrity of the Democracy
in Recent Times’, by discussing developments,
including the persecution of journalists and
independent media and analyzing the
significance and aptness of the laws like UAPA, NRC and CAA. On the other hand, DISEC
focused on the ‘Illicit Trade of Small Arms and Light Weapons’ and the ‘Weaponization of Big
Data’. The motive of the event was to instigate interest among the students in world politics as
well as in various political and civic affairs of our democracy. The event was very useful for
students to develop leadership and public speaking skills.
Chai Pe Charcha
Model United Nations (MUN) club of IIIT-NR
organized a group discussion ‘Chai Pe Charcha’,
on January 19, 2023. The topic of discussion was
‘The State of Media in Contemporary Indian
Democracy and Social Media's Relevance and Role
in Shaping Our Country's Future Politics’. The
participants discussed various aspects like the
independence of media, the neutrality of facts, the
role of media and social media in contemporary
policy, the relevance of social media trends, and
media reforms, among others. Overall, it was a healthy, engaging, and insightful discussion that
enhanced the understanding of the current political and geopolitical scenario of the participants.
74 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍
Annual Report 2022-23
Art and Culture Activities
Cultural Night ‘Mellow Repose’
SAC clubs together organized an electrifying fun-filled
cultural night ‘Mellow Repose’, on May 09, 2022, for the
students to relish the amazing performances by some of the
B. Tech and M. Tech students. The event consisted of
performances from various genres ranging from dance,
singing to literature.
RangDe Aazadi
The cultural club of IIIT-NR, Indradhanush, organized a contest, ‘RangDe Aazadi’, from
August 8-12, 2022, as a part of ‘Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsava’ celebration activities. The theme
of the contest was ‘Patriotism’. The objective of the event was to gauge the participants' thought
processes and awareness of patriotism. It aimed to keep the students engaged, explore and
encourage creativity in students and offer them a platform to showcase their talent. The
participants were given 5 days to showcase their arts. The contest was open to all art forms and
mediums. This event inspired students to think and work creatively in order to promote artistic
excellence.
Azaadi Ke Paar
The theatre club of IIIT-NR, Club De Theatre, organized ‘Azaadi Ke Paar’, on August 09, 2022,
as part of ‘Azaadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav’ celebration activities. In the event students were assigned
a freedom fighter and they were required to enact him/her. The audience was filled with
patriotism which was the main motive of the event.
Bhavarth - Independence Day Quiz
The literature club of IIIT-NR Cover to Cover organized a quiz event called ‘Bhavarth’ on
August 12, 2022, as a part of ‘Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsava’ celebration activities. The topic was
‘Our Country: Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav’. The quiz was held to make students appreciate the
vibrant and long history of our country, with major leaps in cinema, culture, politics, and
administration. The questions spanned the length and breadth of India, with genres like famous
personalities, geography, businesses, and government policies. The questions were thought-
provoking and drawn so as to be engaging and a learning experience for the students.
֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 75

general-annual_report_2022_2023:p085.text:
Annual Report 2022-23
Birsa Munda Quiz
Cover to Cover club of IIIT-NR organized a quiz
event called ‘Birsa Munda’ on the occasion of
Birsa Munda’s Birthday, as a part of “Azadi ka
Amrit Mahotsava” celebrations being conducted
by Student Activity Centre of IIIT-NR. The quiz
was held to make students aware of the history of
tribal leaders in India’s freedom fight.
Ganesh Chaturthi Celebrations
Students, faculty and staff members of IIIT-NR celebrated ‘Ganesh Chaturthi’ in the institute
from August 31 to September 04, 2022. Various cultural programs were organized during these
five days. A mythological quiz named ‘Pratispardha’ was also organized by the ‘Inquisitive’
club. Cultural performances included melodies from members of ‘Capriccio’ club and ground
breaking dance performances by members of ‘Igniters’ club. The 5-day celebrations concluded
with the Visarjan on Sept. 04, 2022.
Rampage
The literary club of IIIT-NR ‘Cover to Cover’ organized an
event ‘Rampage’ on September 13, 2022. In the event, each
participant had to pick a genre, and a topic of their choice
within that genre. They then had to get 2 out of 3 judges to
side with them to win a round. The one who wins the most
rounds was the winner. The participants got to argue for
categories like anime, superhero media, web series, sports,
gaming, etc.
Garba Night Celebration
‘Garba Night’ was organized in the campus by
Student Activity Centre (SAC) on September
30, 2022, as part of the Navratri Celebrations.
Students dressed in Gujarati attires played
garba and displayed their dancing skills.

general-annual_report_2022_2023:p087.text:
Annual Report 2022-23
Rang-Express
The fine art club of IIIT-NR, Indradhanush, organized ‘Rang Express 5.0’, from Dec 13 to 25,
2022 to uncover the talents and to bring out innovative ideas of Batch 2022. The event consisted
of competitions in Sketching, Painting, Digital Art and Craft.
Dance Workshop – Freestyle
The dance club of IIIT-NR, Igniters, conducted a ‘Dance Workshop’ on January 07, 2023,
for introducing the students to the world of dance. The workshop began with demonstration
of different dance moves by the instructor. Participants were encouraged to explore their own
creativity and style while learning the basic steps and techniques. The participants were able
to learn and understand the basics of Freestyle dancing and were able to apply their
knowledge in a creative way.
֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 77
Annual Report 2022-23
Sports and Games Activities
Inter-College Cricket Tournament ‘Aagaaz’
The sports club of IIIT-NR, Atharv, organized
an inter-college cricket tournament, ‘Aagaaz’,
from April 14-17, 2022. Teams from various
institutes of the region, like NIT Raipur, BIT
Raipur, BIT Durg, AIIMS and GEC Bilaspur,
participated in the tournament. IIIT-NR (Team
B) emerged as the winner and NIT-Raipur as
the runner up in this tournament.
Badminton Tournament (Girls)
Sports Club of IIIT-NR Atharv organized a cordial intra
badminton tournament from May 02-05, 2022, to identify
the best badminton players in IIIT-NR.
Treasure Hunt
Inquisitive Club of IIIT-NR organized a treasure hunt competition on May 16, 2022, in the
Institute campus. It was a clue-based treasure hunt competition consisting of two rounds. Each
team had to solve 5 clues to reach the destination. By solving each clue, the team got the location
of the next clue.
LAKSHYA - Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Trophy
SAC (Students Activity Centre) conducted a Sports tournament ‘Lakshya’ from December 14-
15, 2022. The event witnessed 200+ participants in various sports disciplines, including
Football, Cricket, Basketball, Kabaddi, Badminton, Volleyball, Athletics and Table Tennis. The
event was played between 4 teams and the team with the highest points was awarded Shaheed
Veer Narayan Singh trophy, in honour of the Chhattisgarh’s first freedom fighter.
78 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍
Annual Report 2022-23
Aarambh 5.0
Sports Club of IIIT-NR, Atharv, organized the annual intra sports event ‘Aarambh 5.0’, to
discover the best sportspersons in the institute and to promote sports activities in the campus.
The event was inaugurated on January 26, 2023 and was conducted from January 27-29, 2023.
With the help of auction process, all the participants were divided into 4 teams namely (Titans,
Mavericks, Renegades, Spartans), and many sports events were conducted between them, which
included cricket, football, basketball, kabaddi, volleyball, chess, table tennis, badminton
athletics and valorant.
Sports Fest (ASTRA) at IIIT Delhi
IIIT-NR teams participated in ‘Astra23’, a three-
day sports event organized by IIIT Delhi, from
March 24-26, 2023, in which 9 college teams
participated. Our team participated in football
and badminton and gave a good fight to the
opponents.
Social Service and Upliftment Activities
Seminar on ‘Women in Engineering’
IEEE students branch of IIIT-NR, organized a seminar on ‘IEEE Women in Engineering (WIE)-
Towards Technology and Leadership,’ at the institute campus, on April 27, 2022, to promote
women engineers and scientists and inspire girls around the world to motivate them to pursue
their academic career in engineering.
IEEE Women in Engineering (WIE) is one of the largest international professional
organizations, dedicated to promoting women engineers and scientists, which facilitates the
recruitment and retention of women in technical disciplines globally.

general-annual_report_2022_2023:p089.text:
Annual Report 2022-23
NSS Orientation Programme
The National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of IIIT-NR
organized a first-of-its-kind NSS Orientation program for
the B. Tech. Batch 2021, on June 30, 2022. The program
aimed at educating the new NSS volunteers about how
NSS offers excellent opportunities to serve the society and
for personal development.
The event had the presence of Dr. Pradeep Sinha, Director
IIIT-NR; Dr. Neeta Bajpai, NSS Coordinator
Chhattisgarh; Mr. Satyendra Sahu, President Awardee,
NSS Senior Volunteer and Mr. Nikhil Kumar, State
Awardee, Senior NSS Volunteer.
Dr. Sinha in his address to the new NSS Volunteers emphasized the importance of becoming
good human beings in life and not just professionally successful human beings. He encouraged
students to utilize their knowledge and skills for the betterment of society.
Sabka Bharat, Nikharta Bharat
As part of the celebrations to mark the ‘7th Anniversary
of Smart City Mission’, Nava Raipur Atal Nagar Vikas
Pradhikaran (NRANVP), organized an event ‘Sabka
Bharat, Nikharta Bharat’ from June 24-25, 2022. The
event consisted of various competitions like Painting
Competition, Know Your Smart City Quiz, Essay
Writing, Give Your Suggestions (Speech format) and
Debate. The event was organized in Smart Cities around
the country to educate the young masses of the country
about the plans of the mission and also the upcoming
tasks to be done. Teams from institutions like IIM
Raipur, KPS International Naya Raipur, Kalinga
University and many more, participated in the
competitions. IIIT-NR teams won two prizes.
Classes by IIIT-NR for Underprivileged Children
As a part of the ‘Rural Transformation Through
Education Initiative’ of National Service Scheme (NSS),
the NSS unit of IIIT-NR, in collaboration with the
Institute Social Responsibility (ISR) cell conducts weekly
classes in the local schools of Uparwara and Nawagaon villages. The initiative focuses on the
overall personality development of underprivileged students through education, awareness and
physical fitness. The volunteers of various subjects like Mathematics, Basic Sciences,
Humanities etc. take turns visiting the schools every Saturday and Sunday. They also organize
multiple games for the students and spread awareness about the importance of games and sports
for their physical well-being and overall personality development. The drive is a part of various
initiatives taken by NSS, IIIT-Naya Raipur, under the ‘Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav’ celebrations.
80 ֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍
Annual Report 2022-23
Education through Social Work
IIIT-NR conducts various programs as part of its social
responsibility for the development of children of
nearby villages. As part of this, the ISR team of IIIT-
NR distributed stationery items and chocolates to the
children of the Government Primary School,
Nawagaon, Nava Raipur. The team members also
motivated the children for planting trees and educated
them about the importance of plants and how they
should save trees for the benefit of mankind. Mr. R K
Sinha, Head Master of the school, thanked IIIT-NR
team. Panchayat President, Mr. Sujeet Ghidoude, also
expressed his gratitude to the IIIT-NR for such
initiatives.
Awareness Camp on Poshan Abhiyan
Under the aegis of Poshan Abhiyan of the Government
of India, the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of
IIIT-NR, in collaboration with Institute Social
Responsibility (ISR) cell, organized an awareness drive
in the nearby Government School of Nawagaon, Naya
Raipur. The campaign aimed to disseminate knowledge
about the importance of nutrition in our lives and to promote practices that nurture health,
wealth, and immunity to disease and malnutrition. The Poshan Abhiyan is a Government of
India’s flagship program to improve the nutritional outcome for children, adolescent girls,
pregnant women, and lactating mothers. The school administration appreciated the efforts and
contributions of the NSS unit of IIIT-NR towards various schemes such as the Swachchha
Bharat Abhiyaan, Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav, Poshan Abhiyan, and so on, thereby invoking a
sense of responsibility and social service among the volunteers.
Annual Cultural Programme at Learning Centre
The Institute Social Responsibility (ISR) cell of IIIT-NR
organized the Annual Cultural Programme by nearby
village school children studying in the Learning Centre
run by IIIT-NR, on the occasion of Netaji Subhash
Chandra Bose’s Birthday, on January 23, 2023. The
Learning Center at Uparwara, Naya Raipur, named as
‘Vidyasagar - Phule Learning Center’ has been
continuing since 2021. Students, research scholars, and
faculties of IIIT-NR teach at this Learning Center every
Saturday and Sunday with the aim of imparting better
scientific education to village school students. The
programme was attended by faculty, staff, students of
IIIT-NR and the villagers.
֍ IIIT-Naya Raipur | Annual Report | 2022-23 ֍ 81

Annual Report 2022-23
BMC Walkathon
IIIT-NR students participated in a walkathon
organized by Balco Medical Centre, Nava
Raipur on the occasion of its foundation day on
March 23, 2023. The event aimed to raise
awareness about cancer. It began with a
presentation about the disease and its prevalence
in society. The speakers highlighted the
importance of early detection and prevention
measures to fight against cancer. They also
shared some of the current research and progress
being made in the field of cancer treatment. The
presentation was followed by the walkathon.
World Consumer Rights Day 2023
The Student Activity Center (SAC) and National Service Scheme (NSS) of IIIT-Naya Raipur
in association with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Raipur, as part of BIS’s ‘Quality
Connect Campaign 3.0’ conducted a door-to-door survey at its campus at Nava Raipur from
March 15 – 19, 2023, to spread awareness about the importance of standardization. BIS is the
National Standards Body of India, established under the BIS Act 2016 for the harmonious
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and
for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

Anti-Ragging Committee & Policies
In compliance with the decisions of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India and consequent Gazette notification of “University Grant Commission Regulations 2013” for curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions and also as notified by AICTE vide its notification no. 37-3/Legal/AICTE/2009 dated 25-03-2009, the competent authority has constituted following Committees as part of Anti ragging measures in IIITNR campus;
Institute Level Anti-Ragging Committee
VC & Director - Chair
Dean (Academics) - Member
Chairman (HMC)- Member
SAC President - Member
Dr. Sresha Yadav nee Ghosh - Member
Representative of parents (fresher, Senior)
Student representatives (fresher, Senior)
Registrar - Member Secretary
Anti Ragging Flying squads:
The proposed Anti-Ragging Squads shall be empowered to inspect all such places which are vulnerable to incidents of ragging and shall ensure vigil in all such locations. Hostel Level Squad shall also be empowered to inspect all places in the Hostel which are vulnerable to incidents of ragging and shall ensure vigil in all such locations. The Hostel Level Anti-Ragging Squad shall publish the contact information (including Mobile numbers) of it’s members as follows;

Articles of Association of IIIT-NR
ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION
OF
IIIT-NR FOUNDATION FOR TECHNOLOGY BUSINESS INCUBATION &
ENTREPRENEURSHIP
(COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE AND NOT HAVING SHARE CAPITAL
NOT FOR PROFIT UNDER SECTION 8 OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013)
Interpretation
1) The regulations contained in Table ‘H’ of Schedule I of the Companies Act, 2013 shall
apply to this Company. In addition, following articles shall apply in so far as they are not
inconsistent with Table ‘H’.
2) In the interpretation of these articles, unless repugnant to the subject or context:
a) “The Act” means the Companies Act, 2013 or any statutory modifications or re-
enactment thereof for the time being in force.
b) “Annual General Meeting” means a general meeting of the members held in
accordance with the provisions of Section 96 of the Act.
c) “Auditors” means and includes those persons appointed as such by the Company from
time to time.
d) “Board” or “Board of Directors” means the Board of Directors of the Company.
e) “Company” “The Company” or “This Company” means the IIIT-NR FOUNDATION FOR
TECHNOLOGY BUSINESS INCUBATION & ENTREPRENEURSHIP.
f) “Director’s” means the Directors for time being of the Company, or as the case may
be, the directors assembled at a Board.
g) “Extra-ordinary General Meeting” means an extra-ordinary general meeting of the
members duly called and constituted and any adjourned holding thereof.
h) “Member” means a person who agrees in writing to become a member of the
company and whose name is entered in the register of members of the company.
i) “Meeting” or “General Meeting” means a meeting of members.
j) “Month” means a calendar month.
k) “Office” means the Registered Office for the time being of the Company.
l) “Person/s” includes, partnership, company, and association of persons.
m) A “Resolution” shall be an “Ordinary Resolution” when at a General Meeting of which
the notice required under the Act has been duly given, the Votes cast (whether on a
show of hands, or on a poll, as the case may (be) in favour of the resolution (including
the casting vote, if any of the Chairperson) by the members, who being entitled so to
do, vote in person, or where proxies are allowed, by proxy exceed the votes, if any,
cast against the resolution by members so entitled and voting.
n) “Seal” means the Common Seal for the time being of the Company.
o) “Special Resolution” shall have the meaning assigned thereto by Section 189 of the Act.
p) “Written” and “In Writing” including printing, lithography and other modes of
representing or reproducing words in a visible form.
q) Words importing the singular number include, where the context admits or requires,
the plural and vice-versa.
r) Words importing the masculine gender also include the feminine gender.
s) “These presents” or “Regulations” shall means these Articles of Association as
originally framed or altered from time to time and shall include the Memorandum
where context so requires.
t) “Section” or “Sec” means a Section of The Companies Act,2013.
u) “Appellate Tribunal” means the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal constitute
under Section 410 of The Companies Act2013.
3) Unless the context otherwise requires, words or expressions contained in these
regulations shall have the same meaning as in the Act or any statutory modification
thereof in force at the date at which these regulations become binding on the company.
4) The company shall be a “PRIVATE COMPANY” –and accordingly
a) Number of members shall be two excluding
i) persons who are in the employment of the company and
ii) persons who, having been formerly in the employment of the company, were
members and have continued to be members after the employment ceased, shall
not be included in the number of members;
b) Prohibits any invitation to the public to subscribe for any securities of the company.

general-articles_of_association:p002.text:
MEMBERSHIP
5) NUMBER OF MEMBERS
a) The number of members with which the company proposes to be registered is two,
but the board of directors may, from time to time, whenever the company or business
of the company requires it, register an increase of members. Such increase shall be
made through clause amendment of this clause.
b) The subscribers to the Memorandum and such other persons as the Board shall admit
to membership will be members of the company.
6) TERMINATION OF MEMBERSHIP
A member of the Company shall cease to be one on, the happening of any of the following
events:
a) on his becoming bankrupt or if he is found to be of unsound mind or on he is
convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude;
b) on his / its voluntary resignation;
c) on dissolution of the Member Company;
d) if on the recommendation of the Board of Directors, after giving the member an
opportunity to explain at a general meeting of the Company, a majority of three
fourths of the members present thereat, decide that a member has been acting in
derogation of the Company.
7) REGISTER OF MEMBERS
Subject to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 a separate register of members shall
be maintained in which shall be entered the name and address and such other
information about each member as the Board of Directors may from time to time decide.
ADMINISTRATION & MANAGEMENT
8) BOARD OF DIRECTORS
a) The administration of the affairs of the Company shall be vested with the Board of
Directors.
b) Unless otherwise determined by the Company in the General meeting the number of
Directors of the Company shall not be more than fifteen and not less than two.
c) The following persons shall be appointed as Directors of the Company, by virtue of
their office in Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information
Technology, Naya Raipur (IIIT-NR).
These Directors shall hold office of the Directors in the Company, so long as they hold
their office in IIIT-NR.
d) The following shall be the first Director of the Company.
i) Director 1: Dr. Pradeepkumar Manmohan Sinha (Director, IIIT – Naya Raipur)
ii) Director 2: Mr. Krishnarajanagar Gopala Iyenger Srinivasa (Dean (R&I), Professor
(DSAI) IIIT–Naya Raipur
e) The two of the above mentioned First Directors shall hold office of the Director in the
Company, so long as they hold the office in IIIT-NR.
f) The Board shall elect the Chairperson and Vice Chairperson and determine the period
for which they are to hold office.
g) The Board shall have power to co-opt one or more Directors within the maximum
mentioned herein.
h) The remuneration of the directors shall, in so far as it consists of a monthly payment,
be deemed to accrue from day-to-day. Remuneration if any shall be paid to the
directors subject to clause V of the memorandum of association.
i) In addition to the remuneration payable to them in pursuance of the Act, the directors
may be paid all travelling, hotel and other expenses properly incurred by them.
j) In attending the returning from meetings of the Board of Directors or any committee
thereof or general meetings of the Company; or
k) In connection with the business of the company.
8. PROCEEDINGS OF MEETINGS OF BOARD
a) The Board of Directors may meet for the dispatch of business, adjourn and otherwise
regulate its meetings, as it thinks fit.
b) The Chairperson, and in his absence a director shall, at any time, summon a meeting of the
Board.
c) Save as otherwise expressly provided in the Act, questions arising at any meeting of the
Board shall be decided by a majority of votes.
d) In case of equality of votes, the chairperson shall have a second or casting vote.
e) The continuing directors may act notwithstanding any vacancy in the Board but, if and so

general-articles_of_association:p003.text:
long as their number is reduced below the quorum fixed by the Act for a meeting of the
Board, the continuing directors or director may act for the purpose of increasing the
number of directors to the fixed for the quorum, or of summoning a general meeting of
the company, but for no other purpose.
f) The Board may, subject to the provisions of Act, delegate any of its powers to individual
members or committees consisting of such member or members of its body as it thinks
fit.
g) Any committee so formed shall, in the exercise of powers so delegated confirm to any
regulations that may be imposed on its by the Board.
h) A committee may elect a chairperson of its meetings.
i) If no such chairperson is elected, or if at any meeting the chairperson is not present
within five minutes after the time appointed for holding the meeting, the directors
present may choose one of their members to be chairperson of the meeting.
j) A committee may meet and adjourn as it thinks proper.
k) Questions arising at any meeting of the committee shall be determined by a majority of
votes of the members present. And in case of an equality of votes, the chairperson shall
have a second or casting vote.
l) All acts done by any meeting of the Board of committee thereof, or by any person acting
as a director, shall notwithstanding that it may be afterwards discovered that there was
some defect in the appointment of any one or more of such directors or of any person
acting as aforesaid, or that they or any of them were disqualified be as valid as if every
each director or such person had been duly appointed and was qualified to be a director.
m) Save as otherwise expressly provided in the Act, a resolution in writing signed by all the
members of the Board or a committee thereof for the time being entitled to receive
notice of a meeting of the Board or committee, shall be as valid and effectual as if it had
been passed at a meeting of the Board or committee, shall be as valid and effectual as if it
had been passed at a meeting of the Board or committee, duly convened and held.
9. GENERAL MEETINGS AND THE PROCEEDINGS THEREOF
a) All general meetings other than annual general meetings shall be called extraordinary
general meetings.
b) The Board may, whenever it think fit, call an extraordinary general meeting.
c) If at any time there are not within India directors capable of acting, who are sufficient in
number to form a quorum, any director or any two members of the company may call an
extraordinary general meeting in the same manner as nearly as possible, as that in which
such a meeting may be called by the Board.
d) No business shall be transacted at any general meeting unless a quorum of members is
present at the time when the meeting proceeds to business.
e) The quorum requirement for Board meetings shall be either 8 members or 25% of total
strength whichever is less. However, the quorum shall not be less than 2 members as per
the provisions of the companies Act, 2013.
f) If within half an hour from the time appointed for holding the meeting, a quorum is not
present, the meeting, if called upon the requisition of members, shall be dissolved. In any
other case, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the next week, at the
same time and place, or to such other day and at such other time and place as the Board
may determine.
g) If at the adjourned meeting a quorum is not present within half an hour from the time
appointed for the meeting, the members present shall be a quorum.
h) The chairperson may, if any, of the Board shall preside as chairperson at every general
meeting of the company.
i) The chairperson may, with the consent of any meeting at which a quorum is present, and
shall if so directed by the meeting, adjourn the meeting from time to time and from place
to place.
j) No business shall be transacted at any adjourned meeting other than the business left
unfinished at the meeting from which the adjournment took place.
k) In the case of an equality of votes, whether on a show of hands or on a poll, the
chairperson of the meeting at which the show of hands takes place, or at which the poll is
demanded, shall be entitled to a second or casting vote.
l) When a meeting is adjourned for thirty days or more, notice of the adjourned meeting
shall be given as in the case of an original meeting.
m) Save as aforesaid, and as provided in section 103 of the Act, it shall not be necessary to
give any notice of an adjournment or of the business to be transacted at an adjourned
meeting.

general-articles_of_association:p004.text:
10) VOTE OF MEMBERS
a) Every member shall have one vote.
b) A member of unsound mind, or in respect of whom an order has been made by any Court
having jurisdiction in lunacy, may vote, whether on a show of hands or on a poll, by his
committee or other legal guardian, and any such committee or guardian may, on a poll,
vote by proxy.
c) (i) No objection shall be raised to the qualification of any voter except at the meeting or
adjourned meeting at which the vote objected to is given or tendered, and every vote not
disallowed at such meeting shall be valid for all purposes.
(ii) Any such objection made in due time shall be referred to the chairperson of the meeting,
whose decision shall be final and conclusive.
d) A vote given in accordance with the terms of an instrument of proxy shall be valid,
notwithstanding the previous death or insanity of the principal or the revocation of the
proxy or of the authority under which the proxy was executed, or the transfer of the
shares in respect of which the proxy is given; provided that no intimation in writing of
such death, insanity, revocation or transfer shall have been received by the company at its
office before the commencement of the meeting or adjourned meeting at which the
proxy is used.
e) A member may exercise his vote at a meeting by electronic means in accordance with
provisions of the Act and shall vote only once.
f) Any business other than that upon which a poll has been demanded may be proceeded
with, pending the taking of the poll.
11) FUNDS
a) The funds of the Company shall be deposited in Banks and sums as shall not be required
for current expenses, at the discretion of the Board of Directors from time to time shall
operate the accounts of the company with Banks.
b) Subject to the generality of the above the funds that are not immediately required for the
business of the Company shall be invested in accordance with the provisions of The
Income Tax Act,1961.
Chief Executive Officer, Manager, Company Secretary or Chief Financial Officer
12) Subject to the provisions of the Act,
(i) A chief executive officer, manager, company secretary or chief financial officer
may be appointed by the Board for such term, at such remuneration and upon
such conditions as it thinks fit; and any chief executive officer, manager, company
secretary or chief financial officer so appointed may be removed by means of a
resolution of the Board.
(ii) A director may be appointed as chief executive officer, manager, company
secretary or chief financial officer.
13) A provision of the Act or these regulations requiring or authorizing a thing to be done by
or to a director and chief executive officer, manager, company secretary or chief financial
officer shall not be satisfied by its being done by or to the same person acting both as
director and as, or in place of, chief executive officer, manager, company secretary or chief
financial officer.
14) A Secretary may be appointed by the Board for such term at such remuneration and upon
such conditions as it may think fit and the Board may remove the secretary so appointed
and change any terms and conditions as it may think fit.
15) SEAL
a) The Company shall provide for the safe custody of the seal.
b) The Seal of the Company shall not be affixed to any instrument except by the authority of
a resolution of the Company or of a Committee of the Company authorized by it in that
behalf and the seal shall be so affixed in the presence of two Directors of the Board as are
authorized by the Board for this purpose.
c) Deeds, bonds debentures, negotiable instrument and contracts, made on behalf of the
Company and attested and sealed as aforesaid shall be deemed to be duly executed.

general-articles_of_association:p005.text:
16) ARBITRATION
Any dispute arising between any members of the Company in connection with any
business transaction or in connection with the management of the Company or any other
persons that may be referred to the Company or the Company or any dispute between
the company and any of the contractors employed by the Company in connection with
the business of the Company shall be decided by the Arbitration under the rules of the
Company which may be framed for this purpose by the Board of Directors or any sub-
committee authorized by it.
17) INDEMNITY
Every member(s) or office bearer(s) of the Board or any Committee / Sub-Committee and
other officer(s) or servant(s) of the Company for the time being shall be indemnified by
the Company against any loss, damage or misfortune which shall happen in relation in the
execution of the duties of his office unless the same happens through his own dishonesty
or willful neglect or default.
18) SECRECY
A member shall be entitled to inspect the Company’s Books, require discovery of any
information respecting secret process or trade mystery which may relate to the conduct of
the business of the company.
19) DISSOLUTION
Dissolution of the Company shall be as per clause IV of the Object clause of MOA
of the Company.

Board of Governors & Institutional Leadership
Dhananjai Pandey(Chairperson)
A Professor Dhananjai Pandey is an internationally renowned educator and researcher in the field of Materials Science and Technology. His professional career started in 1977 as a Faculty Member in BHU/IIT (BHU) and he retired as Professor (HAG) in 2017 but continued as Institute Professor for another five years. He is presently a Distinguished Professor of BHU (for life) and IIT Bhilai.
A widely travelled scientist, Prof. Pandey has delivered Invited talks/Keynote addresses/ Plenary lectures at very large number of International and National Conferences held within India and abroad. He has published over 200 research articles in journals of international repute, books and book-series with over 8000 citations (14 papers with over 100 citations) and an h-index of 49. He also holds several patents to his credit. He is a Fellow of all the three premier science academies of India (Indian National Science Academy, Indian Academy of Sciences, National Academy of Sciences of India) and a Fellow of the Asia Pacific Academy of Materials. He is a recipient of several awards/medals (INSA Young Scientist Medal, Materials Research Society of India Medal, MRSI Annual Prize and MRSI Distinguished Lectureship award, Homi Bhabha Fellowship Award, DAE Raja Ramanna Award, Pt Jubilee Award of Indian Science Congress, J C Bose National Fellowship award etc). He has
He was Coordinator (Head) of the School of Materials Science and Technology at IT,BHU, first Director in the transition phase and Dean (Faculty Affairs) of IIT BHU. Under his leadership, the School of Mater Sci & Tech emerged as an Internationally reputed Centre of research and teaching in advanced functional materials. As a Dean of Faculty Affairs, policy documents for Salary fixation, Faculty Recruitment and Promotion of deserving existing faculty members as per IIT norms were developed and successfully implemented.
Professor Pandey has been Member of various committees of DST, CSIR, DRDO, UGC, INSA, IASc as well as Member of Governing Body/Council and Executive Council of IIT (BHU), BHU and SU, IUAC etc.
Professor Pandey has been Vice President and President of the Indian Crystallographic Association and Vice President of the Materials Research Society of India and is currently President of the Neutron Scattering Society of India.
Professor Pandey has served as Co-editor of the leading International journals published by the International Union of Crystallography, Acta Crystallographica Section A and Journal of Applied Crystallography (first Indian), and Member of Editorial Boards of International journals (Phase Transitions, Materials Science Forum and Zeitscrift-fur-kristallographie) as well as Indian journals (Bulletin of Materials Science and Praman-a Physics Journal). He presently serves on the editorial advisory boards of Zeitscrift-fur-kristallographie and Bulletin of Materials Science. He has served on many important international bodies like Ewald Prize Committee (the highest award in crystallography) and Asia-Oceania Neutron Scattering Association (AONSA) Prize Committee, Commission on Aperiodic Crystals, Commission on Inorganic Materials and Minerals, Commission on Mathematical and Theoretical Crystallography (MaThCryst), Sub-Committee on Nomenclature for Phase Transitions of the International Union of Crystallography (IUCr). He also served as Chairman of the MaThCryst Commission of the IUCr, being only the third Indian to be elected as Chairman of any one of the IUCr Commissions over the last seven decades. He is a founding Member of EC of AONSA and continues to be its Member from India at present.

Giriraj Nyati
Dr. Giriraj Nyati is a professional with 40+ years of global experience in Engineering & Technology, Research, Operations, SCM, Strategy & Leadership. A PhD holder from IIT Delhi, with BE (Electrical & Electronics) from BITS, Pilani & MBA from Sukhadia University, Udaipur, Dr Nyati, brings on rich international experience of working with fortune 500 companies & Nobel laureates like Nakamura San. He was associated with Genus Power Infrastructure Limited & Secure Meters as COO & Moser Baer as CTO. Dr Nyati had been instrumental in joint envisioning & driving R&D projects related to Optical data storage, semiconductor & display technologies. He is credited with bringing technologies of strategic importance to country, setting up of highly advanced world class manufacturing operations & achieving less than 100 ppm defect level quality and reliability standards.
Dr Nyati is India’s one of the known technology experts in renewable energy & was the chairman of 5 government committees constituted by the Department of Electronics & Information technology related to nanotechnology based next generation solar cells. He is also the co -inventor of the “Light Scribe” technology & was awarded the FICCI best prize for “Technology & Innovation” in the year 2010 by then Finance minister, Mr Pranab Mukherjee. Dr Nyati had been instrumental in deploying a disruptive model for the benefits of the tribal belt of Rajasthan that resulted in the employment of over 1000 females from extremely poor strata of the society.

Steven A. Pinto
Steven A. Pinto is a retired Lead Director on the Chairman's Supervisory Board of the Emirates Investment Bank, UAE. He is currently serving on the Boards of ACGL, a Tata Motors subsidiary, Easyaccess Finance, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Redington India, Adlabs Entertainment Limited and CRIF High Mark. In the year 2000, he was appointed CEO of Osool Finance Company and concurrently Head of Retail Banking at Mashreq Bank, Dubai.
He is an Economics Honors graduate with a Masters in Management from the University of Mumbai.

Rajiv Prakash
Prof. Rajiv Prakash is the Director of IIT Bhilai. He was appointed to this position by the Hon’ble President of India in her capacity as the Visitor of IIT Bhilai. A Professor of Materials Science and Technology at IIT (BHU) Varanasi, Prof. Prakash has held several key academic and administrative responsibilities, including Head of the School of Materials Science and Technology (twice), Dean (R&D), founder coordinator of the Central Instrument Facility, and IPR Cell of the Institute.
He has made major translational contributions in sensor and biosensor engineering by integrating conducting polymers, nanomaterials, smartphone-based diagnostics, IoT-enabled sensing, and automated analysis. His technologies include field-deployable systems for arsenic detection in water, PSA-based cancer diagnostics, glucose sensing, and point-of-care platforms for kidney-related biomarkers and sickle-cell anaemia. Several of these technologies have reached advanced readiness levels and have been transferred to industry. His broader engineering contributions also include polymer composites for optical storage and railway applications, corrosion protection using conducting polymers and green inhibitors, charge-storage materials, and materials for green-energy applications.
Prof. Prakash has published more than 270 refereed journal papers (Google Scholar h-index of 53), holds 25 patents (with 3 technology transfer). His recognitions include the Young Scientist Award, INAE Young Engineer Award, MRSI Medal, election as Academician of the Asia Pacific Academy of Materials, and the Lifetime Engineering Excellence Award 2025 from The Institution of Engineers (India), Bhilai. As Director of IIT Bhilai and Chairman of IIT Bhilai Innovation and Technology Foundation (IBITF), a DST NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hub, he has advanced innovation-led institutional growth. His recent leadership contributions include AI-enabled Vidya Samiksha Kendra initiatives for data-driven school governance in Chhattisgarh, the proposed IT Park in Durg, and the Tribal Research and Innovation Park (TRIP) in Bastar, which seeks to integrate deep-tech solutions with traditional knowledge for sustainable livelihood and regional development.

He has made major translational contributions in sensor and biosensor engineering by integrating conducting polymers, nanomaterials, smartphone-based diagnostics, IoT-enabled sensing, and automated analysis. His technologies include field-deployable systems for arsenic detection in water, PSA-based cancer diagnostics, glucose sensing, and point-of-care platforms for kidney-related biomarkers and sickle-cell anaemia. Dr. Mukul Sutaone is currently the Director of Indian Institute of Information Technology, Allahabad (An Institute of National Importance with the Act of Parliament). In the immediate past, he graced the position of the First Vice Chancellor of COEP Technological University Pune, which is the legacy in the field of Engineering Education in the Country. He worked at College of Engineering, Pune (COEP) as Professor in Electronics and Telecommunication department for more than 30 years, with illustrious accomplishments in Academics and Research. At COEP, Prof. Sutaone handled various administrative responsibilities such as Officiating Director, Deputy Director, Dean Academics, Dean- International Relations, Head of the Department, etc.
His areas of work & interests in Teaching & Research are 'Statistical & Adaptive Signal Processing, Wireless Communication & Networks and Statistical Modeling of Data'. He has conceived, practiced, executed and steered many innovative academic experiments in curriculum design and delivery for the students and faculty of his Institute, Pune University and other aspiring institutes, mentored by him.
In the capacity of Principal investigator of the "Center of Excellence in Signal & Image Processing", a World Bank funded project by MHRD-GoI (under TEQIP), Prof. Sutaone has been associated with the development and conversion of prototypes from mere Proof of Concept (PoC) to transferrable technologies. Some of such projects are ‘Video Stabilization for Cell Phones’ ‘Automated Inspection System for PCB fault detection’, ‘Density and Direction detection for Stampedes’, and 'Optimal Microphone Array for Audio beam-forming'.
With handsome number of contributed and cited publications to his credit, a few granted patents and copyrights as well as multiple Govt./Corporate funded projects, he is an applauded resource person in many conferences, workshops and symposia, in the areas of Signal Processing, Next Generation Communication, Outcome based Education and Effective Deployment of New Education Policies. Prof. Sutaone is recipient of Prof. SVC Aiya IETE National Award for Excellence in Telecomm.

Neeraj Jalota
Shri Neeraj Jalota is a senior power sector professional with over 37 years of distinguished experience encompassing project development, operations, maintenance, and coal mining. He holds an M.Tech in Industrial Engineering from IIT Delhi and a Post Graduate Diploma in Business Management from MDI Gurgaon, reflecting a strong blend of technical depth and managerial leadership.
Currently, Shri Jalota serves as the Executive Director, Unified Shared Services Centre (USSC), an integrated single-window platform responsible for materials procurement and contract management for NTPC stations nationwide. In this role, he has played a pivotal part in driving process standardization, operational efficiency, and enterprise-wide integration of shared services.
In addition, he holds the responsibility of Regional Executive Director (WR-II), as the administrative head of five major thermal power stations located at Korba, Sipat, and Lara in Chhattisgarh, and Gadarwara and Khargone in Madhya Pradesh. His mandate encompasses oversight of Operations and Maintenance activities for an aggregate operating capacity of 10,100 MW, as well as strategic supervision of ongoing capacity expansion projects totaling 4,000 MW, including 1,600 MW each at Lara and Gadarwara, and 800 MW at Sipat.
Prior to his current roles, Shri Jalota served as Chief Executive Officer of the Jhabua Thermal Power Plant, where he successfully transformed the captive power plant into a profitable operation, strengthened environmental compliance, and enhanced overall operational performance.
He has undergone several in-house and overseas training programmes in technical, managerial, and mining domains. Shri Jalota’s vast leadership experience, institutional perspective, and strategic insight contribute meaningfully to governance and capacity-building initiatives.

Premlata
Ms. Premlata is a seasoned HR leader with over 35 years of distinguished experience in the Indian power sector, encompassing Thermal, Hydro, Gas, Joint Ventures and taken-over power projects across India. Having joined NTPC as an Executive Trainee, she has held a wide range of leadership positions throughout her career and brings deep expertise across the entire spectrum of Human Resource Management.
She currently serves as the Executive Director (Strategic HRD & Talent Development) & Head NTPC-PMI, where she leads the organisation's enterprise-wide agenda on competency development, learning and development, leadership nurturing, and capability building. In this capacity, she is spearheading initiatives aimed at developing a future-ready, agile, and high-performing workforce aligned with NTPC's strategic priorities and its transition towards a sustainable energy future.
She also serves as Chairperson of the Governing Council of NTPC School of Business, providing strategic direction to strengthen management education and leadership development within the evolving energy ecosystem.
Over the years, she has played a pivotal role in advancing NTPC's talent and leadership development agenda through innovative interventions in succession planning, digital learning, reskilling and upskilling. Her contributions have been instrumental in translating business strategy into workforce capabilities, enabling organisational excellence and long-term growth.
She is serving on the Boards of two NTPC-affiliated companies and as NTPC Nodal Officer for WePOWER – Women in Energy, a World Bank-supported network in South Asian Region.

general-board_of_governors:p011.text:
Prof. (Dr.) Om Prakash Vyas is a distinguished academician, researcher, and institutional leader with over three decades of experience in technical education, research, and academic administration. He holds an M.Tech. in Computer Science from IIT Kharagpur and pursued doctoral research at Technical University of Kaiserslautern, Germany, under a DAAD Fellowship.
As the founding Head of Computer Science at Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University, he established Chhattisgarh’s first formal Computer Science programme in 1992. His early initiatives played a pioneering role in extending Computer Science and IT education across a large network of affiliated colleges in Chhattisgarh, helping lay the foundation for the State’s subsequent expansion of IT education.
Prof. Vyas has had a long and significant association with IIIT Allahabad, beginning as Assistant Professor during 2002–03, in the formative years of the Institute. He returned to IIIT-A in 2009 as Professor of Information Technology and continued there until 2026, serving in several academic and leadership responsibilities, including as Dean (Research & Development), Dean (Technology Development) and Member of BoG. During this period, he contributed to the Institute’s academic development, including the conceptualization and introduction of the B.Tech. programme in IT–Business Informatics in 2019, and coordinated NEP 2020-inspired academic reforms for B.Tech. programs.
He has successfully led several national and international collaborative research projects and has been a sought-after Visiting Professor at multiple global institutions. These include the National Institute of Informatics, Tokyo (Japan, 2010), the University of Paderborn (Germany, 2013–2017), Inria Lille (France, 2015), the University of Messina (Italy, 2016), Norwegian Technical University (Norway), and Bielefeld University (Germany, 2018–2023), where he taught and conducted research every summer for five consecutive years.
As Vice Chancellor and Director of IIIT-Naya Raipur, Prof. Vyas has successfully implemented an NEP 2020-inspired B.Tech. curriculum with a flexible Major–Minor structure, enabling students across engineering branches to pursue interdisciplinary Minors including Business Informatics, Digital Mobility, Digital Humanities, Cyber Security, and Quantum Computing. His leadership emphasizes research excellence, innovation, multidisciplinary education, and industry–academia and international collaboration.
His academic interests span Data Science, Process Intelligence, Business Informatics, Explainable AI, Cyber Security, and Agentic AI. He is currently pursuing international research collaborations in Agentic AI through Indo-Italian initiatives and Cyber Security for Critical Infrastructure through Indo-Norwegian projects.

general-institute_faqs:p001.text:
Official Institute FAQs
To which university and technical board the Institute is affiliated?
The Institute in itself is a State University established by the Government of Chhattisgarh and recognized by UGC.
When was the institute established?
The first academic session of the institute commenced from Aug 2015 in its own campus.
What are the programs offered?
The Institute currently offers the following programs:-
a) 4 Years B.Tech. in (ECE)
b)4 Years B.Tech. in (CSE)
c)4 Years B.Tech. in (DSAI)
d)2 Years M.Tech. in (CSE)
e)2 Years M.Tech. in (ECE)
f) Ph.D. in (ECE)
g) Ph.D. in (CSE)
h) Ph.D. in (Physics)
i) Ph.D. in (Mathematics)
j) Ph.D. in (English)
k) Ph.D. in (Management)
When does admission for B.Tech programs begin?
The admission to B.Tech programs begins in May-June.
What is the admission criteria for B.Tech. programs?
Admission to the undergraduate program of the DSPM IIIT-NR is based strictly on the merit of the candidate as inferred from their performance in JEE (Joint Entrance Examination). The minimum eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under Chhattisgarh quota at IIIT-NR is 50% aggregate marks in Physics and Mathematics (45% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD candidates) in their 12th standard examination. The eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under All India category and NTPC quota is as per JoSAA guidelines.
Is Ph.D. offered at IIIT-NR?
Yes. Please visit Admission section at our website for further details.
When does admission for Ph.D. programs begin?
The admission for Ph.D. programs usually takes place at the beginning of each semester (i.e June for Autumn semester and December for Spring semester)
Is ragging prohibited in IIIT-NR?
Ragging of any kind is strictly prohibited in the Institution. As per the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, if any incident of ragging comes to the notice of the authorities, the concerned student will be given liberty to explain and if his explanation is not found satisfactory, he or she will be expelled from the Institution.
Are there any scholarships available for B.Tech students?
Are there any seats reserved for female candidates?
For admission to its programs under CG Quota , the institute follows the Chhattisgarh State Government policy on reservation of 30% to Women. However , for admission under All India Quota & NTPC , Government of India policy on reservation applies.
What are the documents required to be submitted at the time of admission?
Please follow instructions available on the website as part of the application process.
How many students will be admitted to B.Tech. program ?
Please see the Admission Brochure.
What is the strength of faculty?
The Institute currently has 27 regular faculty members, with more joining in July 2019. In addition , there are adjunct and visiting faculty members too.
Is hostel facility available? Are day-scholars allowed?
Yes, there are three Boys hostels and one Girls hostel. All programs offered by IIIT-NR are fully residential. It is mandatory for all students to stay on campus, even if the student is from the Naya Raipur region. Hostel facilities for 1025 students (785 boys & 240 girls) are currently available.
What is minimum cut-off for application to B.Tech. programs?
There is no minimum cut-off of JEE Main Merit rankings.
Will IIIT Naya Raipur admission happen through JoSAA?
Yes w.e.f from 2017. Kindly visit JoSAA website at institute code 420. Admission through JoSAA is for All India Quota ( 35% seats).
When will online applications for admission begin?
Refer to the schedule announced.

general-institute_faqs:p002.text:
Can I apply under both All India quota and Chhattishgarh state quota?
Yes, through JoSAA in case of All India quota and through our web portal if you are eligible under Chhattishgarh state quota.
What is the best chance of getting a seat at IIIT-NR while choice filling in JoSAA portal?
Select the choice of programs available at IIIT-NR (Institute code 420) as first ,second and Third choices.
What is Admission under other categories?
Other categories mean admissions under a) 50 % seats under Chhattishgarh State Quota b) 15 % seats under NTPC quota.
How do I apply under State quota?
After initial login at our admission portal, you will be asked to fill the requisite form.
Is there any fee for application? If so, how to pay?
Yes, candidates have to pay Rs.500/- online through admission portal.
Can I fill choices without application fee?
No. You will be able fill in choices only after successful fee payment.
How should I order the choices of academic programs?
You must fill your choices of academic program in the DECREASING order of preferences. That is, your most preferred one should be on the top.
Will a candidate be allowed to reshuffle the choice list at any stage of seat allotment?
Candidates are allowed to reshuffle/reorder their choices ONLY during choice filling period before they “lock” their choices. Beyond that there is NO option of reordering.
What is locking of choices? Once locked, can I unlock?
Lock is an option indicating the finalization of choices. Choices will be automatically locked on the last date of application.
What is the period of choice filling?
Refer to the schedule announced.
Is there any cut off marks for registration and choice?
Yes, The eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under Chhattisgarh quota at IIIT-NR is 50% aggregate marks in Physics and Mathematics (45% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD candidates) in their 12th standard examination. The eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under All India category and NTPC quota is as per JoSAA guidelines.
How many rounds of seat allotment will happen?
Three rounds
What if seats remain vacant after three rounds? Will they be filled on quota or category basis?
Seats remaining vacant at the end of three rounds of counseling, under any quota or reserved category shall be converted to All-India General(Open) and shall be available for admissions in the Spot Round.

Admission to the undergraduate program of the DSPM IIIT-NR is based strictly on the merit of the candidate as inferred from
their performance in JEE (Joint Entrance Examination). The minimum eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under
Chhattisgarh quota at IIIT-NR is 50% aggregate marks in Physics and Mathematics (45% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD candidates) in
their 12th standard examination. The eligibility for applying for the B.Tech program under All India category and NTPC quota
is as per JoSAA guidelines.
Is Ph.D. offered at IIIT-NR?
Yes. Please visit Admission section at our website for further details.
When does admission for Ph.D. programs begin?
The admission for Ph.D. programs usually takes place at the beginning of each semester (i.e June for Autumn semester and
December for Spring semester)
Is ragging prohibited in IIIT-NR?
Ragging of any kind is strictly prohibited in the Institution. As per the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, if any
incident of ragging comes to the notice of the authorities, the concerned student will be given liberty to explain and if his
explanation is not found satisfactory, he or she will be expelled from the Institution.
Are there any scholarships available for B.Tech students?
Financial aid to the needy students is under active consideration of the Govt. Of Chhattisgarh. Any student entitled for
financial aid as approved by the Govt. will get back to the refund from already paid fees.
Are there any seats reserved for female candidates?
For admission to its programs under CG Quota , the institute follows the Chhattisgarh State Government policy on
reservation of 30% to Women. However , for admission under All India Quota & NTPC , Government of India policy on
reservation applies.
What are the documents required to be submitted at the time of admission?
Please follow instructions available on the website as part of the application process.
How many students will be admitted to B.Tech. program ?
Please see the Admission Brochure.
What is the strength of faculty?
The Institute currently has 27 regular faculty members, with more joining in July 2019. In addition , there are adjunct and
visiting faculty members too.
Is hostel facility available? Are day-scholars allowed?
Yes, there are three Boys hostels and one Girls hostel. All programs offered by IIIT-NR are fully residential. It is mandatory for
all students to stay on campus, even if the student is from the Naya Raipur region. Hostel facilities for 1025 students (785
boys & 240 girls) are currently available.
What is minimum cut-off for application to B.Tech. programs?
There is no minimum cut-off of JEE Main Merit rankings.
Will IIIT Naya Raipur admission happen through JoSAA?
Yes w.e.f from 2017. Kindly visit JoSAA website at institute code 420. Admission through JoSAA is for All India Quota ( 35%
seats).

डॉ. श्यामाप्रसाद मुखर्जी अंतरराष्ट्रीय सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी संस्थान

Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Next Generation Networks
Objective:
To promote research and innovation in this highly promising area, IIIT Nava Raipur has setup a
5G testbed in its CoE. The CoE has been established in line with Govt. of India’s goal to build
indigenous testbeds that closely resemble real-world 5G deployments.
Lab Facilities & Equipment:
This 5G waveform generation and analysis reference solution combine hardware, software and
measurement expertise providing the essential components of a flexible 5G waveform
generation and analysis test platform. The reference solution enables engineers and researchers
to generate and analyze a variety of 3GPP 5G NR waveforms at RF, centimeter-wave, and
millimeter-wave frequencies with modulation bandwidths of up to 2 GHz, with an emphasis on
5G 3GPP NR activity in the 28 GHz and 37 - 39 GHz bands. 5G testbed includes Signal Analyzer (2
Hz to 50 GHz), Vector signal generator (250 kHz to 44 GHz), Arbitrary Waveform Generator (14
Bit / 8GSa/s and 12 Bit / 12 GSa/s), Oscilloscope (1 GHz 4 channel) and other basic facilities. IIIT-
NR has also developed the anechoic chamber for characterization, configurable software like
SystemVue, MATLAB, and Labview. It also has Multi GPU SMP Server to incorporate machine
learning applications in communication This will encourage Indian startups and industries to
take an early lead in 5G technology. This testbed is first of its kind not only in Chhattisgarh but in
Central India. IIIT-NR is now among the few premier institutions in India like IIT-Madras, IISc-
Bangalore, IIT-Kanpur, IIT-Delhi, IIT-Hyderabad and SAMEER-Mumbai, which have their own 5G
testbed.
Key Achievements:
 Conducted workshop on
o Robotics & Artificial Intelligence using MATLAB, March 4-6, 2020
o Evolution of Cognitive Radio Networks and Its Relevance in 5G: From Theory to
Practice, Jan 23-26, 2020
o Workshop on Cognitive radio, Aug 5-7, 2019
o Physical Layer Techniques of 5G Wireless Communication, May 7-11, 2018
 Participate in telecommunications standards development society (TSDSI), india
 Submitted project proposal worth more than 10 crore
o NM-ICPS with IIIT Bangalore, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Bhilai, Advanced Communication
System
o Meity with IIT Patna, Design & Development of Energy-Aware 3D-MIMO with
Massive Antennas for 5G Enhanced Mobile Broadband using Machine Learning
algorithm
o SERB, Joint parameter estimation and symbol detection in OFDM based IoT
Networks: Machine Learning based approaches
 Submitted proposal to conduct workshop in high reputed international conference
o Orchestration of 5G Network & beyond using Machine Learning (O5ML 2020) in
conjunction with WCNC, April 6-9, 2020
 Collaborate with external Industry and academia in India & abroad
o IIT, IIITs
o University College Dublin
Page 2 of 8
Artificial Intelligence and Deep Leaning (AIDL) lab
Objective:
AIDL lab established to carries out work on a variety of topics within Artificial Intelligence and
Machine Learning with a focus on using real world problems to discover computationally hard
problems of modelling uncertainty, learning predictive models and enabling decision making. It
also provides computing platform for novel languages like Python, R, and OpenCV and other
necessary for building coherent set of ideas, fundamental of Machine Learning, Artificial
Intelligence and Deep Learning models and algorithms.
Lab Facilities & Equipment:
It has a Multi GPU Server equipped with processors are high-end 2 x Intel® Scalable processors
Xeon 6148 and dual GeForce GTX 1080TI (11GB) with total SSD Storage of server 30 x 4000GB.
Lab includes 10 Multi GPU workstations equipped with 2 x Intel® Scalable processors Xeon 4114
with 64GB (Max 1024GB) of memory, 8TB of disk space and dual GeForce GTX 1080TI (11GB).
Key Achievements:
 Conducted workshop on data science, machine learning and artificial intelligence etc
o ATAL workshop on deep learning
o Workshop on machine learning and AI
 Singed MOU
o with industry like Farmguide, Delhi
o with Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalay (IGKV), Raipur
 Ongoing
o DST, Artificial Intelligence and IoT Based UAV System for Crop Health
Monitoring and Forecasting, 24 lakhs, 2020-2022
o TEQIP, Real-Time Detection, Classification and Remedy of Invasive Insects in
Soybean Crop Through Deep Learning Technique
o TEQIP, Use of Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning in Identification of Major
Disorders Important Crops
o TEQIP, Use of Block Chain to Assure Quality of Farm Inputs (Seed, Planting
Material, Fertilizer Etc)
 Submitted project proposal worth more than 1.5 crore
o Joint project submission with COEP Pune
o SERB, 5G, IoT and Artificial Intelligence based wearable devices for health
monitoring and forecasting
o IMPRESS, ICSSR, Target insects early identification and labeling in crop using
deep learning techniques: Smart Agriculture
o IMPRESS, ICSSR, Immediate healthcare support using intelligent accident
detection through surveillance video
Page 3 of 8

Internet of Things (IoT) and Sensor lab
Objective:
The IoTs lab provides necessary software, equipment to develop, and characterization of novel
smart sensors for IoT applications.
Lab Facilities & Equipment:
Along with these the lab is equipped with various kits like Smart Healthcare, Smart Agriculture,
Smart Village and City. The main research is focused on development of a wide range of
wearable sensors for pervasive monitoring, self-powered sensor nodes through energy
harvesting and implementation of IoT based solution in in the area of healthcare, agriculture,
and environment through the introduction of novel sensing platforms and ICT approaches.
Through fusing multiple sensing modalities, we aim to develop a smart environment, which can
learn and adapt to different environments and provide proactive sensing for different
applications.
Key Achievements:
 Conducting workshop on IoT, Sensor etc
o Robotics & Artificial Intelligence using MATLAB, March 4-6, 2020
o Sensor network, IoT and Internet of everything, Dec 13-15, 2019
o FDP on "Internet of Things”, July 2018
 Conduct event SCInTFIC annually for school students for past three years
